questions.t: Answer the following about circles. Where the answer involves π, give the exact value and also the value correct to 2 decimal places.
p: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm.
Find the radius of a circle whose area is 36π cm<sup>2</sup>.
Find the radius of a circle whose area is 20 cm<sup>2</sup>, correct to 2 decimal places.
ap: A = π × 7<sup>2</sup> = 49π cm<sup>2</sup> ≈ 153.94 cm<sup>2</sup>.
π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = 36π, so <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = 36 and <var>r</var> = 6 cm.
πr2 = 20, so r2 = 20π ≈ 6.3662, giving r ≈ 2.52 cm.

questions.t: Find the area of each sector, giving the exact value and the value correct to 2 decimal places.
p: a sector of a circle of radius 12 cm with an angle of 150° at the centre
a quarter of a circle of radius 9 m
ap: A = 150360 × π × 122 = 512 × 144π = 60π cm2 ≈ 188.50 cm2.
A = 14 × π × 92 = 20.25π m2 ≈ 63.62 m2.

questions.t: A window is made of one sheet of glass in the shape of a rectangle 80 cm wide and 120 cm high, with a semicircle of diameter 80 cm sitting on top of the rectangle. Find the total area of the glass, in exact form and then correct to the nearest square centimetre.
questions.a: Rectangle: 80 × 120 = 9600 cm<sup>2</sup>. Semicircle has radius 40 cm, so its area is ½ × π × 40<sup>2</sup> = 800π cm<sup>2</sup>. Total = (9600 + 800π) cm<sup>2</sup> ≈ 9600 + 2513.27 = 12 113.27, so about 12 113 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A circle is drawn inside a square of side length 20 cm so that the circle touches all four sides of the square. Find the area of the region that is inside the square but outside the circle, in exact form and correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.a: The circle touches all four sides, so its diameter is 20 cm and its radius is 10 cm. Area = 20<sup>2</sup> − π × 10<sup>2</sup> = (400 − 100π) cm<sup>2</sup> ≈ 400 − 314.16 = 85.84 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A rectangular prism has dimensions 9 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm.
p: Find the surface area of the closed prism.
The prism is an open box with no lid, the 9 cm by 6 cm face being the base. Find the total area of its five faces.
ap: Remove one 9 cm by 6 cm face (the lid): 228 − 54 = 174 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A prism 20 cm long has a uniform cross-section that is a right-angled triangle whose two shorter sides are 5 cm and 12 cm.
p: Find the length of the hypotenuse of the cross-section.
Find the total surface area of the prism.
ap: <var>h</var><sup>2</sup> = 5<sup>2</sup> + 12<sup>2</sup> = 25 + 144 = 169, so the hypotenuse is 13 cm.
Two triangular ends: 2 × ½ × 5 × 12 = 60 cm<sup>2</sup>. Three rectangular faces: (5 + 12 + 13) × 20 = 30 × 20 = 600 cm<sup>2</sup>. Total surface area = 60 + 600 = 660 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A cylinder has base radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. Give each answer in exact form and correct to 2 decimal places.
p: Find the surface area of the closed cylinder.
Find the surface area of the same cylinder if it is open at the top, so only one circular end is counted.
questions.al: Curved surface = 2π<var>r</var><var>h</var> = 2π × 4 × 10 = 80π cm<sup>2</sup>; each circular end = π × 4<sup>2</sup> = 16π cm<sup>2</sup>.
ap: S = 80π + 16π = 96π cm<sup>2</sup> ≈ 301.59 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A cylindrical water tank has an internal diameter of 2.4 m and an internal height of 1.8 m.
p: Find the volume of the tank in cubic metres, correct to 2 decimal places.
Find how many litres the tank holds when full, correct to the nearest 100 litres.
ap: The radius is 1.2 m, so V = π × 1.2<sup>2</sup> × 1.8 = 2.592π ≈ 8.14 m<sup>3</sup>.
1 m<sup>3</sup> = 1000 L, so the capacity is 8.1430 × 1000 ≈ 8143 L, which is 8100 L to the nearest 100 litres.

questions.t: Convert each measurement into the unit shown, expressing every answer in scientific notation.
p: 45 micrometres, in metres
320 nanoseconds, in seconds
one hour, in microseconds
ap: 1 micrometre = 10<sup>−6</sup> m, so 45 μm = 45 × 10<sup>−6</sup> = 4.5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> m.
1 nanosecond = 10<sup>−9</sup> s, so 320 ns = 320 × 10<sup>−9</sup> = 3.2 × 10<sup>−7</sup> s.
One hour = 3600 s, and 1 s = 10<sup>6</sup> μs, so one hour = 3600 × 10<sup>6</sup> = 3.6 × 10<sup>9</sup> μs.

questions.t: A solid metal cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. A cylindrical hole of radius 2 cm is drilled right through it along its axis, so the hole has the same axis as the cylinder. Find the volume of the remaining solid, in exact form and correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the missing measurement in each solid.
p: A cylinder of base radius 6 cm has volume 800 cm<sup>3</sup>. Find its height, correct to 2 decimal places.
A cube has volume 3.375 m<sup>3</sup>. Find the length of one of its edges.
ap: π × 62 × h = 800, so 36πh = 800 and h = 80036π ≈ 7.07 cm.
<var>a</var><sup>3</sup> = 3.375, so <var>a</var> = 1.5 m (since 1.5<sup>3</sup> = 3.375).

questions.t: A rectangular shed measuring 12 m by 8 m stands in the middle of a large level lawn. A goat is tethered by a 10 m rope to a ring fixed at one outside corner of the shed. The rope is taut when stretched and cannot pass through the shed, so it bends around a corner when the goat walks past it. Find the total area of lawn the goat can reach, in exact form and correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.a: At the ring the two walls take up a right angle, so the goat sweeps 270360 = 34 of a circle of radius 10 m: 34 × π × 102 = 75π m2. Walking around the corner 8 m away, 10 − 8 = 2 m of rope is left, giving a quarter circle of radius 2 m: 14 × π × 22 = π m2. Around the corner 12 m away no rope is left, since 10 < 12, so nothing is added there. Total area = 75π + π = 76π m2 ≈ 238.76 m2.

questions.t: A swimming pool is a prism whose uniform cross-section is a trapezium. Measured along its length the pool is 12 m from end to end, it is 6 m wide, and the top edge is level all the way round. The pool is 1 m deep at the shallow end and 2.5 m deep at the deep end, the floor sloping evenly between them.
p: The pool is filled with water to a level 0.2 m below the top edge. Find the volume of water in the pool, in kilolitres.
Later the water level is 0.3 m below the top edge. Find how many litres of water have been lost.
ap: The water surface is level, so the water is a prism with a trapezoidal cross-section of depths 1 − 0.2 = 0.8 m and 2.5 − 0.2 = 2.3 m, with 12 m between them. Cross-sectional area = ½(0.8 + 2.3) × 12 = ½ × 3.1 × 12 = 18.6 m<sup>2</sup>. Volume = 18.6 × 6 = 111.6 m<sup>3</sup> = 111.6 kL (111 600 L).

Now the depths are 0.7 m and 2.2 m, so the area is ½(0.7 + 2.2) × 12 = 17.4 m<sup>2</sup> and the volume is 17.4 × 6 = 104.4 m<sup>3</sup>. Water lost = 111.6 − 104.4 = 7.2 m<sup>3</sup> = 7200 L. (Check: the level dropped 0.1 m over a surface of 12 × 6 = 72 m<sup>2</sup>, and 72 × 0.1 = 7.2 m<sup>3</sup>.)

questions.t: A foam drink-can holder is a cylinder that is open at the top. The cavity inside it is a cylinder of radius 4 cm and depth 10 cm. The foam wall is 1 cm thick all the way round and the foam base is 1 cm thick, so the outside of the holder is a cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 11 cm. Give each answer in exact form and correct to 2 decimal places.
p: Find the volume of foam in the holder.
A drink can exactly fills the cavity. Find the total area of foam that is still exposed, counting the outside curved surface, the outside of the base, and the flat ring of foam around the top rim.
ap: Volume of foam = outer cylinder − cavity = π × 5<sup>2</sup> × 11 − π × 4<sup>2</sup> × 10 = 275π − 160π = 115π cm<sup>3</sup> ≈ 361.28 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Outside curved surface = 2π × 5 × 11 = 110π cm<sup>2</sup>; outside of base = π × 5<sup>2</sup> = 25π cm<sup>2</sup>; top ring = π(5<sup>2</sup> − 4<sup>2</sup>) = 9π cm<sup>2</sup>. Total = 110π + 25π + 9π = 144π cm<sup>2</sup> ≈ 452.39 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A skate ramp is a trough in the shape of a half-cylinder: its cross-section is a semicircle, and the ramp is 6 m long. The curved part of the cross-section, that is the semicircular arc, has length 9.5 m.
p: Find the radius of the half-cylinder, correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the width of the ramp across the top of the trough, correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the area of the curved surface of the ramp.
ap: The semicircular arc has length πr, so πr = 9.5 and r = 9.5π ≈ 3.02 m.
The width across the top is the diameter, 2r = 19π ≈ 6.05 m.
Unrolled, the curved surface is a rectangle 9.5 m by 6 m, so its area is 9.5 × 6 = 57 m<sup>2</sup> exactly.

questions.t: Three faces of a rectangular prism that meet at one vertex have areas 24 cm<sup>2</sup>, 32 cm<sup>2</sup> and 48 cm<sup>2</sup>.
p: Find the volume of the prism.
Find the three dimensions of the prism.
questions.al: Let the dimensions be <var>x</var>, <var>y</var>, <var>z</var> with <var>xy</var> = 24, <var>yz</var> = 32 and <var>zx</var> = 48.
ap: Multiplying: (<var>xyz</var>)<sup>2</sup> = 24 × 32 × 48 = 36 864, so <var>xyz</var> = 192. The volume is 192 cm<sup>3</sup>.
x = 19232 = 6 cm, y = 19248 = 4 cm, z = 19224 = 8 cm. Check: 6 × 4 = 24, 4 × 8 = 32, 8 × 6 = 48.

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a trapezium in which <var>AB</var> is parallel to <var>DC</var>, with <var>AB</var> = <var>a</var> and <var>DC</var> = <var>c</var>. The point <var>E</var> is the midpoint of <var>AD</var>, the point <var>F</var> is the midpoint of <var>BC</var>, and <var>EF</var> = <var>k</var>. The distance between the parallel sides <var>AB</var> and <var>DC</var> is <var>h</var>.
p: Show that <var>k</var> = ½(<var>a</var> + <var>c</var>).
Hence show that the area of the trapezium equals <var>kh</var>.
ap: <var>EF</var> is parallel to the two parallel sides. Draw the diagonal <var>AC</var> and let it meet <var>EF</var> at <var>M</var>. In △<var>ACD</var>, <var>E</var> is the midpoint of <var>AD</var> and <var>EM</var> is parallel to <var>DC</var>, so <var>M</var> is the midpoint of <var>AC</var> and <var>EM</var> = ½<var>c</var>. In △<var>ABC</var>, <var>M</var> is the midpoint of <var>AC</var> and <var>MF</var> is parallel to <var>AB</var>, so <var>MF</var> = ½<var>a</var>. Hence <var>k</var> = <var>EM</var> + <var>MF</var> = ½<var>c</var> + ½<var>a</var> = ½(<var>a</var> + <var>c</var>).

Area = ½(<var>a</var> + <var>c</var>)<var>h</var> = ½(<var>a</var> + <var>c</var>) × <var>h</var> = <var>kh</var>. Any correct argument earns full marks, for example using the midpoint theorem on the diagonal <var>BD</var> instead of <var>AC</var>.

questions.t: Solve each equation.
p: (<var>x</var> − 7)(<var>x</var> + 2) = 0
<var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 9) = 0
ap: <var>x</var> − 7 = 0 or <var>x</var> + 2 = 0, so <var>x</var> = 7 or <var>x</var> = −2.
<var>x</var> = 0 or <var>x</var> = −9.
2x − 5 = 0 or 3x + 1 = 0, so x = 52 or x = −13.

questions.t: Solve each quadratic equation by factorising.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var> − 15 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 9<var>x</var> + 20 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 3<var>x</var> = 40
ap: (<var>x</var> + 5)(<var>x</var> − 3) = 0, so <var>x</var> = −5 or <var>x</var> = 3.
(<var>x</var> − 4)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 4 or <var>x</var> = 5.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 3<var>x</var> − 40 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 8)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0 and <var>x</var> = −8 or <var>x</var> = 5.

questions.t: Solve each equation, first dividing both sides by the numerical common factor.
p: 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 36<var>x</var> = 0
3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 18<var>x</var> + 24 = 0
−<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 13<var>x</var> − 42 = 0
ap: Dividing by 4: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 9<var>x</var> = 0, so <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> − 9) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 0 or <var>x</var> = 9.
Dividing by 3: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 8 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 2)(<var>x</var> − 4) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 2 or <var>x</var> = 4.
Dividing by −1: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 13<var>x</var> + 42 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 6)(<var>x</var> − 7) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 6 or <var>x</var> = 7.

questions.t: Solve each equation.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 81 = 0
25<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 9 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 14<var>x</var> + 49 = 0
ap: (<var>x</var> − 9)(<var>x</var> + 9) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 9 or <var>x</var> = −9.
25x2 = 9, so x2 = 925 and x = 35 or x = −35.
(<var>x</var> + 7)<sup>2</sup> = 0, so there is only one solution, <var>x</var> = −7.

questions.t: Solve each quadratic equation.
p: 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 7<var>x</var> + 3 = 0
3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 11<var>x</var> − 4 = 0
6<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> = 5<var>x</var> + 6
ap: Product 6, sum −7, so split as −x − 6x: 2x2 − x − 6x + 3 = x(2x − 1) − 3(2x − 1) = (2x − 1)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 12 or x = 3.
Product −12, sum 11, so split as 12x − x: (3x − 1)(x + 4) = 0, so x = 13 or x = −4.
6x2 − 5x − 6 = 0. Product −36, sum −5, so split as −9x + 4x: (2x − 3)(3x + 2) = 0, so x = 32 or x = −23.

questions.t: Solve each equation by first expanding and collecting all the terms on one side.
p: <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 4) = 45
(<var>x</var> − 1)(<var>x</var> + 6) = 18
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 4<var>x</var> − 45 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 9)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0 and <var>x</var> = −9 or <var>x</var> = 5.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>x</var> − 6 = 18, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>x</var> − 24 = 0 and (<var>x</var> + 8)(<var>x</var> − 3) = 0, giving <var>x</var> = −8 or <var>x</var> = 3.

questions.t: Solve each equation. Assume that <var>x</var> cannot take a value that makes a denominator zero.
p: x + 24x = 11
x − 34 = 7x
ap: Multiplying both sides by <var>x</var>: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 24 = 11<var>x</var>, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>x</var> + 24 = 0 and (<var>x</var> − 3)(<var>x</var> − 8) = 0, giving <var>x</var> = 3 or <var>x</var> = 8.

Cross-multiplying: <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> − 3) = 28, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 3<var>x</var> − 28 = 0 and (<var>x</var> − 7)(<var>x</var> + 4) = 0, giving <var>x</var> = 7 or <var>x</var> = −4.

questions.t: Solve x + 52 − 4x + 1 = 1.
questions.a: Multiply both sides by 2(x + 1): (x + 5)(x + 1) − 8 = 2(x + 1). Expanding, x2 + 6x + 5 − 8 = 2x + 2, so x2 + 6x − 3 = 2x + 2 and x2 + 4x − 5 = 0. Then (x + 5)(x − 1) = 0, so x = −5 or x = 1. Neither makes x + 1 equal zero. Check x = 1: 62 − 42 = 3 − 2 = 1. Check x = −5: 02 − 4−4 = 0 + 1 = 1.

questions.t: A rectangular photograph is 5 cm longer than it is wide and its area is 84 cm<sup>2</sup>. Let the width be <var>x</var> cm. Write down a quadratic equation and solve it to find the width and the length of the photograph.
questions.a: The length is (<var>x</var> + 5) cm, so <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 5) = 84, giving <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>x</var> − 84 = 0. Then (<var>x</var> + 12)(<var>x</var> − 7) = 0, so <var>x</var> = −12 or <var>x</var> = 7. A width cannot be negative, so <var>x</var> = 7. The width is 7 cm and the length is 12 cm. Check: 7 × 12 = 84.

questions.t: Each term of the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, … is obtained by adding 4 to the previous term. The sum <var>S</var> of the first <var>n</var> terms is given by <var>S</var> = 2<var>n</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>n</var>. How many terms must be added to give a sum of 168?
questions.a: 2n2 + 5n = 168, so 2n2 + 5n − 168 = 0. Product 2 × (−168) = −336 and sum 5, so the numbers are 21 and −16: 2n2 + 21n − 16n − 168 = n(2n + 21) − 8(2n + 21) = (2n + 21)(n − 8) = 0. So n = −212 or n = 8. Since n must be a positive whole number, n = 8. Check: 7 + 11 + 15 + 19 + 23 + 27 + 31 + 35 = 168.

questions.t: Consider the parabola <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 2<var>x</var> − 3.
p: Find the value of <var>y</var> when <var>x</var> = −1, and the value of <var>y</var> when <var>x</var> = 4.
Find the coordinates of the two points where the parabola crosses the <var>x</var>-axis.
The axis of symmetry lies midway between those two points. Write down its equation and hence find the coordinates of the vertex.
ap: When <var>x</var> = −1, <var>y</var> = 1 + 2 − 3 = 0. When <var>x</var> = 4, <var>y</var> = 16 − 8 − 3 = 5.
Put <var>y</var> = 0: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 2<var>x</var> − 3 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 3)(<var>x</var> + 1) = 0 and the points are (3, 0) and (−1, 0).
Midway between <var>x</var> = −1 and <var>x</var> = 3 is <var>x</var> = 1, so the axis of symmetry is <var>x</var> = 1. When <var>x</var> = 1, <var>y</var> = 1 − 2 − 3 = −4, so the vertex is (1, −4).

questions.t: Solve each equation by completing the square, giving exact answers.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 2 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 10<var>x</var> − 4 = 0
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 9 − 9 + 2 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> − 7 = 0 and (<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 7. Hence <var>x</var> − 3 = √7 or <var>x</var> − 3 = −√7, so <var>x</var> = 3 + √7 or <var>x</var> = 3 − √7.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 10<var>x</var> + 25 − 25 − 4 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 5)<sup>2</sup> = 29 and <var>x</var> = −5 + √29 or <var>x</var> = −5 − √29.

questions.t: Consider the quadratic <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> + 11.
p: By completing the square, write the rule in the form <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> − <var>h</var>)<sup>2</sup> + <var>k</var>.
State the coordinates of the turning point and the equation of the axis of symmetry.
Find the <var>y</var>-intercept and the exact <var>x</var>-intercepts of the graph.
ap: <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> + 16 − 16 + 11 = (<var>x</var> − 4)<sup>2</sup> − 5.
The turning point is (4, −5) and the axis of symmetry is <var>x</var> = 4.

When <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = 11, so the <var>y</var>-intercept is (0, 11). When <var>y</var> = 0, (<var>x</var> − 4)<sup>2</sup> = 5, so <var>x</var> = 4 + √5 or <var>x</var> = 4 − √5. The <var>x</var>-intercepts are (4 + √5, 0) and (4 − √5, 0), that is about (6.24, 0) and (1.76, 0).

questions.t: By completing the square, show that the equation <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> + 11 = 0 has no solutions.
questions.a: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> + 9 − 9 + 11 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> + 2 = 0 and hence (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> = −2. But a square is never negative: (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> ≥ 0 for every value of <var>x</var>, so (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> can never equal −2. Therefore the equation has no solutions. (Equivalently, <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> + 11 = (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> + 2 ≥ 2 for all <var>x</var>, so it is never zero.)

questions.t: A circular table top is pushed into the corner of a rectangular room so that its edge just touches both walls. A point <var>P</var> on the edge of the table top is 8 cm from one wall and 1 cm from the other wall. Let the radius of the table top be <var>r</var> cm; the centre of the table is then <var>r</var> cm from each wall.
p: Take the corner of the room as the origin and the two walls as the axes, so the centre of the table is at (<var>r</var>, <var>r</var>) and <var>P</var> is at (1, 8). Show that <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> − 18<var>r</var> + 65 = 0.
Find the two possible values of <var>r</var>.
For the larger of the two tables, find the exact distance from the corner of the room to the centre of the table, and give it correct to one decimal place.
ap: <var>P</var> lies on the edge of the table, so its distance from the centre is <var>r</var>: (1 − <var>r</var>)<sup>2</sup> + (8 − <var>r</var>)<sup>2</sup> = <var>r</var><sup>2</sup>. Expanding, 1 − 2<var>r</var> + <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + 64 − 16<var>r</var> + <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = <var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, so <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> − 18<var>r</var> + 65 = 0.

(<var>r</var> − 5)(<var>r</var> − 13) = 0, so <var>r</var> = 5 or <var>r</var> = 13. Both are geometrically possible: for <var>r</var> = 5, 4<sup>2</sup> + 3<sup>2</sup> = 25; for <var>r</var> = 13, 12<sup>2</sup> + 5<sup>2</sup> = 169.
The larger table has <var>r</var> = 13, so its centre is at (13, 13). The distance from the corner is √(13<sup>2</sup> + 13<sup>2</sup>) = 13√2 ≈ 18.4 cm.

questions.t: A rectangular box has the property that if its length is increased by 1 cm, its width by 2 cm and its height by 3 cm, it becomes a cube whose volume is 496 cm<sup>3</sup> greater than the volume of the box. Let the edge of the cube be <var>s</var> cm. Find <var>s</var> and the three dimensions of the original box.
questions.a: The box measures (<var>s</var> − 1) cm by (<var>s</var> − 2) cm by (<var>s</var> − 3) cm, so <var>s</var><sup>3</sup> − (<var>s</var> − 1)(<var>s</var> − 2)(<var>s</var> − 3) = 496. Since (<var>s</var> − 1)(<var>s</var> − 2)(<var>s</var> − 3) = <var>s</var><sup>3</sup> − 6<var>s</var><sup>2</sup> + 11<var>s</var> − 6, this gives 6<var>s</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>s</var> + 6 = 496, so 6<var>s</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>s</var> − 490 = 0. Product 6 × (−490) = −2940 and sum −11, so split as 49<var>s</var> − 60<var>s</var>: <var>s</var>(6<var>s</var> + 49) − 10(6<var>s</var> + 49) = (6<var>s</var> + 49)(<var>s</var> − 10) = 0. A length cannot be negative, so <var>s</var> = 10. The cube has edge 10 cm and the box is 9 cm by 8 cm by 7 cm. Check: 1000 − 504 = 496.

questions.t: A rectangular garden bed of area 36 m<sup>2</sup> is divided into three identical rectangular sections by two straight dividers, each divider running right across the width of the bed. Each section is <var>x</var> m wide, so the whole bed is 3<var>x</var> m long, and the bed is <var>y</var> m wide (so each divider is <var>y</var> m long). Edging is laid all the way around the outside of the bed and along both dividers, and 34 m of edging is used altogether.
p: Explain why 3<var>xy</var> = 36 and why 6<var>x</var> + 4<var>y</var> = 34.
Show that 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 17<var>x</var> + 24 = 0.
Find both possible sets of dimensions for the whole garden bed.
ap: The bed is 3<var>x</var> m by <var>y</var> m, so its area is 3<var>xy</var> = 36. The edging around the outside is the perimeter, 2(3<var>x</var>) + 2<var>y</var> = 6<var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var>, and the two dividers add another 2<var>y</var>, giving 6<var>x</var> + 4<var>y</var> = 34.
From the area, xy = 12, so y = 12x. Halving the edging equation gives 3x + 2y = 17, so 3x + 24x = 17. Multiplying by x: 3x2 + 24 = 17x, that is 3x2 − 17x + 24 = 0.

Product 72, sum −17, so split as −8x − 9x: (3x − 8)(x − 3) = 0, giving x = 83 or x = 3. If x = 3 then y = 4 and the bed is 9 m by 4 m. If x = 83 then y = 4.5 and the bed is 8 m by 4.5 m. Both fit: 9 × 4 = 36 with edging 18 + 16 = 34, and 8 × 4.5 = 36 with edging 16 + 18 = 34.

questions.t: A rectangular lawn is <var>a</var> m long and <var>b</var> m wide. A path of uniform width <var>x</var> m is laid all the way around the outside of the lawn.
p: Show that the area of the path, in square metres, is 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var>(<var>a</var> + <var>b</var>).
The lawn is 24 m long and 40 m wide. Write the area of the path in terms of <var>x</var>.
The path in part b has area 272 m<sup>2</sup>. Find <var>x</var>.
ap: The lawn and the path together form a rectangle (<var>a</var> + 2<var>x</var>) m by (<var>b</var> + 2<var>x</var>) m, so the area of the path is (<var>a</var> + 2<var>x</var>)(<var>b</var> + 2<var>x</var>) − <var>ab</var> = <var>ab</var> + 2<var>ax</var> + 2<var>bx</var> + 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>ab</var> = 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var>(<var>a</var> + <var>b</var>).
With <var>a</var> = 24 and <var>b</var> = 40, the area is 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var> × 64 = 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 128<var>x</var> m<sup>2</sup>.

4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 128<var>x</var> = 272. Dividing by 4: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 32<var>x</var> − 68 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 34)(<var>x</var> − 2) = 0 and <var>x</var> = −34 or <var>x</var> = 2. A width must be positive, so <var>x</var> = 2 m. Check: 28 × 44 − 24 × 40 = 1232 − 960 = 272.

questions.t: A diagonal of a polygon is a line segment joining a vertex to a non-adjacent vertex. A polygon with n sides has n(n − 3)2 diagonals.
p: How many diagonals has a 12-sided polygon?
A polygon has 170 diagonals. How many sides has it?
Show that no polygon has exactly 100 diagonals.
ap: 12 × 92 = 54 diagonals.
n(n − 3)2 = 170, so n(n − 3) = 340 and n2 − 3n − 340 = 0. Then (n − 20)(n + 17) = 0, so n = 20 or n = −17. A polygon cannot have a negative number of sides, so it has 20 sides. Check: 20 × 172 = 170.

We would need n2 − 3n − 200 = 0, and no two whole numbers have product −200 and sum −3. Completing the square, (n − 32)2 = 200 + 94 = 8094, so n = 3 + √8092 ≈ 15.7, which is not a whole number. Indeed a 15-sided polygon has 15 × 122 = 90 diagonals and a 16-sided polygon has 16 × 132 = 104, and the count increases with n, so it jumps from 90 straight to 104 and 100 is never reached.

questions.t: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of length 25 cm and an area of 84 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the lengths of the other two sides.
questions.a: Let the two shorter sides be p cm and q cm. By Pythagoras' theorem p2 + q2 = 252 = 625, and the area gives 12pq = 84, so pq = 168. Then (p + q)2 = p2 + 2pq + q2 = 625 + 336 = 961, so p + q = 31 (the sides are positive). Hence q = 31 − p and p(31 − p) = 168, giving p2 − 31p + 168 = 0 and (p − 7)(p − 24) = 0. So p = 7 and q = 24 (or the other way round): the two sides are 7 cm and 24 cm. Check: 72 + 242 = 49 + 576 = 625 and 12 × 7 × 24 = 84.

questions.t: Priya cycles at a constant speed of 12 km/h for 25 minutes. How far does she cycle? Give your answer in metres.
questions.a: Distance = 12 × 2560 = 5 km = 5000 m.

questions.t: Convert each rate to the units asked for.
p: 72 km/h into metres per second
15 m/s into kilometres per hour
ap: 72 km/h = 72 000 m/h = 720003600 = 20 m/s.

questions.t: Find each average speed.
p: A train travels 210 km in 1 hour 30 minutes. Give the average speed in kilometres per hour.
Sam walks 1.8 km in 20 minutes. Give his average speed in metres per second.
ap: 1 h 30 min = 1.5 h, so average speed = 210 ÷ 1.5 = 140 km/h.
1.8 km = 1800 m and 20 min = 1200 s, so average speed = 1800 ÷ 1200 = 1.5 m/s.

questions.t: A truck travels at a constant speed of 75 km/h.
p: Write a formula for the distance <var>d</var> kilometres travelled by the truck in <var>t</var> hours.
State the gradient of the straight-line graph of <var>d</var> against <var>t</var>.
ap: In 1 hour the truck travels 75 km, so <var>d</var> = 75<var>t</var>.
The gradient is 75 (the speed in km/h).

questions.t: Write each of these statements using the symbol ∝.
p: The volume <var>V</var> cubic centimetres of a cube is directly proportional to the cube of its side length <var>s</var> centimetres.
The distance <var>d</var> kilometres to the visible horizon is directly proportional to the square root of the height <var>h</var> metres above sea level.
ap: <var>V</var> ∝ <var>s</var><sup>3</sup>.
<var>d</var> ∝ √<var>h</var>.

questions.t: In each case find the formula connecting the two pronumerals. All values are positive.
p: <var>a</var> ∝ <var>b</var>, and <var>a</var> = 21 when <var>b</var> = 3
<var>m</var> ∝ <var>n</var><sup>2</sup>, and <var>m</var> = 18 when <var>n</var> = 3
<var>y</var> ∝ √<var>x</var>, and <var>y</var> = 12 when <var>x</var> = 9
ap: <var>a</var> = <var>kb</var>, so 21 = 3<var>k</var>, <var>k</var> = 7 and <var>a</var> = 7<var>b</var>.
<var>m</var> = <var>kn</var><sup>2</sup>, so 18 = 9<var>k</var>, <var>k</var> = 2 and <var>m</var> = 2<var>n</var><sup>2</sup>.
<var>y</var> = <var>k</var>√<var>x</var>, so 12 = 3<var>k</var>, <var>k</var> = 4 and <var>y</var> = 4√<var>x</var>.

questions.t: A tank that holds a maximum of 50 L of water already contains 8 L. Water then flows in at a constant rate of 6 L per minute. Let <var>V</var> litres be the volume of water in the tank <var>t</var> minutes after the flow begins.
p: Give the formula for <var>V</var> in terms of <var>t</var>.
State the values of <var>t</var> for which this formula applies.
ap: The graph is a straight line with gradient 6 and <var>V</var>-axis intercept 8, so <var>V</var> = 6<var>t</var> + 8.
The tank is full when 6<var>t</var> + 8 = 50, that is <var>t</var> = 7, so the formula applies for 0 ≤ <var>t</var> ≤ 7.

questions.t: Yasmin cycles towards a town at a constant 15 km/h. She starts at a point 45 km from the town. Let <var>d</var> kilometres be her distance from the town after <var>t</var> hours.
p: Give a formula for <var>d</var> in terms of <var>t</var>.
State the gradient and the vertical axis intercept of the graph of <var>d</var> against <var>t</var>.
State the values of <var>t</var> for which the formula applies.
She starts riding at 9:30 a.m. At what time does she reach the town?
ap: She is 45 km away at <var>t</var> = 0 and loses 15 km of distance each hour, so <var>d</var> = 45 − 15<var>t</var>.
Gradient −15, vertical axis intercept 45.
<var>d</var> = 0 when <var>t</var> = 3, so 0 ≤ <var>t</var> ≤ 3.
The ride takes 3 hours, so she arrives at 12:30 p.m.

questions.t: The cost $<var>C</var> of a fence is directly proportional to its length <var>L</var> metres. A fence 24 m long costs $1080.
p: Find the formula for <var>C</var> in terms of <var>L</var>.
Find the cost of a fence 37 m long.
ap: <var>C</var> = <var>kL</var>, so 1080 = 24<var>k</var> and <var>k</var> = 45. Thus <var>C</var> = 45<var>L</var>.
When <var>L</var> = 37, <var>C</var> = 45 × 37 = 1665, so the fence costs $1665.

questions.t: Given that <var>y</var> ∝ <var>x</var><sup>3</sup>, state the effect on <var>y</var> when <var>x</var> is:
p: multiplied by 4
divided by 2
questions.al: <var>y</var> = <var>kx</var><sup>3</sup>. Take <var>x</var> = 1, giving <var>y</var> = <var>k</var>.
ap: <var>x</var> = 4 gives <var>y</var> = 64<var>k</var>, so <var>y</var> is multiplied by 64.
x = ½ gives y = k8, so y is divided by 8.

questions.t: The power <var>P</var> kilowatts needed to drive a boat is directly proportional to the cube of its speed <var>v</var> metres per second. A power of 250 kW drives the boat at 5 m/s.
p: Find the formula for <var>P</var> in terms of <var>v</var>.
Find the power needed to drive the boat at 7 m/s.
Find, correct to 2 decimal places, the speed of the boat when 400 kW is used.
ap: <var>P</var> = <var>kv</var><sup>3</sup>, so 250 = <var>k</var> × 125 and <var>k</var> = 2. Thus <var>P</var> = 2<var>v</var><sup>3</sup>.
400 = 2<var>v</var><sup>3</sup>, so <var>v</var><sup>3</sup> = 200 and <var>v</var> = ∛200 ≈ 5.85 m/s.

questions.t: Answer each part, giving exact percentages.
p: Given that <var>a</var> ∝ <var>b</var><sup>2</sup>, find the percentage change in <var>a</var> when <var>b</var> is increased by 10%.
Given that <var>y</var> ∝ √<var>x</var>, find the percentage change in <var>x</var> when <var>y</var> is decreased by 25%.
ap: <var>a</var> = <var>kb</var><sup>2</sup>. Take <var>b</var> = 1, so <var>a</var> = <var>k</var>. When <var>b</var> = 1.1, <var>a</var> = 1.21<var>k</var>, which is 121% of the previous value, so <var>a</var> increases by 21%.

<var>y</var> = <var>k</var>√<var>x</var>, so squaring gives <var>y</var><sup>2</sup> = <var>k</var><sup>2</sup><var>x</var>, that is <var>x</var> ∝ <var>y</var><sup>2</sup>. Take <var>y</var> = 1 and <var>x</var> = 1. When <var>y</var> = 0.75, <var>x</var> is multiplied by 0.75<sup>2</sup> = 0.5625, which is 56.25% of the previous value, so <var>x</var> decreases by 43.75%.

questions.t: Suppose <var>p</var> ∝ <var>r</var> and <var>q</var> ∝ <var>r</var>, where <var>p</var>, <var>q</var> and <var>r</var> are positive and <var>p</var> > <var>q</var> for every value of <var>r</var>.
p: Prove that <var>p</var> − <var>q</var> is directly proportional to <var>r</var>.
Prove that <var>pq</var> is directly proportional to <var>r</var><sup>2</sup>.
questions.al: Write <var>p</var> = <var>k</var><sub>1</sub><var>r</var> and <var>q</var> = <var>k</var><sub>2</sub><var>r</var> for positive constants <var>k</var><sub>1</sub>, <var>k</var><sub>2</sub>. Since <var>p</var> > <var>q</var>, <var>k</var><sub>1</sub> > <var>k</var><sub>2</sub>.
ap: <var>p</var> − <var>q</var> = (<var>k</var><sub>1</sub> − <var>k</var><sub>2</sub>)<var>r</var>, and <var>k</var><sub>1</sub> − <var>k</var><sub>2</sub> is a positive constant, so <var>p</var> − <var>q</var> ∝ <var>r</var>.

<var>pq</var> = <var>k</var><sub>1</sub><var>k</var><sub>2</sub><var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, and <var>k</var><sub>1</sub><var>k</var><sub>2</sub> is a positive constant, so <var>pq</var> ∝ <var>r</var><sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: It is known that a is directly proportional to x2, that b is directly proportional to 1x, and that y = a + b. It is found that y = 7 when x = 1, and also that y = 7 when x = 2.
p: Find an expression for <var>y</var> in terms of <var>x</var>.
Hence find <var>y</var> when <var>x</var> = 3.
ap: Write a = px2 and b = qx, so y = px2 + qx. When x = 1: p + q = 7. When x = 2: 4p + q2 = 7, that is 8p + q = 14. Subtracting gives 7p = 7, so p = 1 and q = 6. Hence y = x2 + 6x.
When <var>x</var> = 3, <var>y</var> = 9 + 2 = 11.

questions.t: A truck leaves a depot at 9 a.m. and travels along a highway at a constant 70 km/h. A car leaves the same depot at 11 a.m. and travels along the same highway at a constant 105 km/h.
p: At what time does the car catch up with the truck?
How far from the depot are they at that moment?
ap: At 11 a.m. the truck has travelled 2 × 70 = 140 km. The car gains 105 − 70 = 35 km each hour, so it needs 140 ÷ 35 = 4 hours. The car catches the truck at 3 p.m.
Distance = 105 × 4 = 420 km from the depot (check: the truck has travelled 70 × 6 = 420 km).

questions.t: Two aeroplanes pass each other in flight while travelling in opposite directions. Each plane keeps flying for a further 40 minutes, after which they are 840 km apart. The speed of the slower plane is 23 of the speed of the faster plane. Calculate the average speed of each aeroplane.
questions.a: Let the faster speed be v km/h; the slower is 2v3 km/h. In 40 min = 23 h the total distance apart is 23(v + 2v3) = 23 × 5v3 = 10v9. So 10v9 = 840, giving v = 756. The planes average 756 km/h and 504 km/h. (Check: 504 km + 336 km = 840 km.)

questions.t: For gemstones of the same quality, the value of a stone is directly proportional to the square of its weight. A stone worth $<var>C</var> is cut into two pieces.
p: Show that if the weights of the two pieces are in the ratio 2 : 3, the loss in value is 12C25.
Show that if the weights are in the ratio <var>a</var> : <var>b</var>, the loss in value is 2<var>abC</var> ÷ (<var>a</var> + <var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.al: Let a stone of weight <var>w</var> have value <var>kw</var><sup>2</sup>, so <var>C</var> = <var>kw</var><sup>2</sup> for the original stone.
ap: The pieces weigh 2w5 and 3w5, so their total value is kw2(425 + 925) = 1325kw2 = 13C25. The loss is C − 13C25 = 12C25.

The pieces weigh awa + b and bwa + b, so their total value is kw2(a2 + b2) ÷ (a + b)2 = C(a2 + b2) ÷ (a + b)2. The loss is C − C(a2 + b2) ÷ (a + b)2 = C[(a + b)2 − a2 − b2] ÷ (a + b)2 = 2abC ÷ (a + b)2, as required.

questions.t: A sales representative leaves town A at noon and drives towards town B, which is 240 km away. She covers 90 km during the first hour, then stops for exactly one hour, then drives the remaining distance at a constant speed, reaching town B at 4 p.m.
p: Find her speed during the third hour of the journey, that is between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m.
Find her average speed for the whole journey from noon to 4 p.m.
Find the time at which she was first 50 km from town B.
ap: She has 240 − 90 = 150 km left, driven between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m., so her speed is 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h.
Average speed = 2404 = 60 km/h.
Being 50 km from B means being 190 km from A, so she must cover 100 km after 2 p.m. This takes 100 ÷ 75 = 43 hours = 1 hour 20 minutes, so the time is 3:20 p.m.

questions.t: Priya recorded the number of text messages she sent on each of eight days: 7, 12, 9, 7, 15, 11, 7, 14. Find each of the following.
p: the mean
the median
the mode
the range
ap: In order: 7, 7, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15. With 8 values the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values: (9 + 11) ÷ 2 = 10
mode = 7 (it occurs three times)
range = 15 − 7 = 8

questions.t: In a survey of 20 households, 3 households owned no pets, 6 owned 1 pet, 7 owned 2 pets, 3 owned 3 pets and 1 owned 4 pets. Find each of the following for the number of pets per household.
p: the mean, correct to 2 decimal places
the median
the mode
ap: The median lies in the (20 + 1) ÷ 2 = 10.5th position, so it is the average of the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative counts are 3, 9, 16, 19, 20, so both the 10th and 11th values are 2. Median = 2
mode = 2 (highest frequency, 7)

questions.t:
The times, in minutes, taken by 18 students to finish a puzzle were:
24, 31, 18, 27, 35, 22, 19, 41, 33, 28, 26, 37, 15, 30, 24, 39, 22, 45
p: Present this information on a stem-and-leaf plot, using the tens digit as the stem.
Which 10-minute group contains the most students, and how many students are in it?
Find the median time.
ap:
Stem 1: leaves 5, 8, 9
Stem 2: leaves 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 7, 8
Stem 3: leaves 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9
Stem 4: leaves 1, 5
(1 | 5 means 15 minutes)
The 20–29 group, with 7 students.
In order: 15, 18, 19, 22, 22, 24, 24, 26, 27, 28, 30, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 45. With 18 values the median is the average of the 9th and 10th values: (27 + 28) ÷ 2 = 27.5 minutes

questions.t:
The numbers of runs scored by a cricketer in each of 20 innings were:
4, 17, 23, 8, 35, 41, 12, 26, 19, 7, 33, 28, 15, 44, 21, 9, 38, 24, 11, 30
p: Present this information in a frequency table using the class intervals 0–9, 10–19, 20–29, 30–39, 40–49.
In how many innings did he score fewer than 20 runs?
In how many innings did he score at least 30 runs?
Explain why the exact mean number of runs cannot be found from your frequency table alone.
ap: 4 + 5 = 9 innings
4 + 2 = 6 innings

Grouping the data into classes loses the individual values — the table only tells us how many scores fall in each class, not what those scores were, so the exact total (and hence the exact mean) cannot be recovered.

questions.t: A histogram of the marks of a group of Year 9 students in a science test has the following columns: 40–49, 8 students; 50–59, 14 students; 60–69, 20 students; 70–79, 12 students; 80–89, 5 students; 90–99, 1 student.
p: How many students sat the test?
If the pass mark was 60, what percentage of students passed? Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
Which class contains the median mark?
Describe the shape of the distribution.
ap: The median is in the (60 + 1) ÷ 2 = 30.5th position, i.e. the average of the 30th and 31st marks. Cumulative counts are 8, 22, 42, so both lie in the 60–69 class.
The distribution has a peak at 60–69 with a long tail to the right (only 6 students above 79) and a short tail to the left, so it is positively skewed.

questions.t:
Two walking clubs each have 12 members. Their ages are shown in a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot with the tens digit as the stem.
Club Pine: stem 1, leaves 5, 8; stem 2, leaves 0, 2, 4, 7; stem 3, leaves 1, 3, 8; stem 4, leaves 2, 6; stem 5, leaf 4.
Club Quarry: stem 1, no leaves; stem 2, leaves 3, 6; stem 3, leaves 0, 4, 5, 9; stem 4, leaves 1, 2, 7; stem 5, leaves 0, 3, 8.
p: How many members of each club are under 30?
Find the range of ages for each club.
Find the median age for each club, and use these to say which club has the older membership.
ap: Pine: 2 + 4 = 6 members; Quarry: 0 + 2 = 2 members
Pine: 54 − 15 = 39 years; Quarry: 58 − 23 = 35 years

With 12 values the median is the average of the 6th and 7th values. Pine: (27 + 31) ÷ 2 = 29 years. Quarry: (39 + 41) ÷ 2 = 40 years. Club Quarry has the older membership, since its median age of 40 is 11 years above Club Pine's median of 29.

questions.t: Answer both of the following.
p: The mean of the five numbers 13, 18, <var>x</var>, 24 and 30 is 21. Find <var>x</var>.
The mean of six numbers is 14. A seventh number is included and the mean of all seven numbers is 15. Find the seventh number.
ap: Sum of the five numbers = 5 × 21 = 105. Also 13 + 18 + 24 + 30 = 85, so <var>x</var> = 105 − 85 = 20.
Sum of the six numbers = 6 × 14 = 84. Sum of the seven numbers = 7 × 15 = 105. The seventh number = 105 − 84 = 21.

questions.t: Part-way through a season a batter has scores of 24, 61, 38 and 17. Assume she is dismissed in every innings.
p: Calculate her batting average so far.
Her average after her next innings is 38. How many runs did she score in that innings?
She plays 10 innings in the season altogether and wants an average of 45 at the end of the season. How many runs must she score in total in her remaining 5 innings?
ap: After 5 innings the total must be 5 × 38 = 190, so she scored 190 − 140 = 50 runs.
For an average of 45 over 10 innings she needs a total of 10 × 45 = 450 runs. She has 190 after 5 innings, so she needs 450 − 190 = 260 runs in the remaining 5 innings.

questions.t:
A stem-and-leaf plot records the masses, in kilograms, of the students in a class, using the tens digit as the stem:
Stem 4: leaves 2, 5, 7, 8
Stem 5: leaves 0, 1, 3, 3, 6, 8, 9
Stem 6: leaves 0, 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9
Stem 7: leaves 1, 3
(6 | 4 means 64 kg)
p: How many students are in the class?
Find the median mass.
Find the range of the masses.
Find the mode or modes.
ap: 4 + 7 + 8 + 2 = 21 students
The median is in the (21 + 1) ÷ 2 = 11th position. The stem 4 row covers positions 1–4 and the stem 5 row covers positions 5–11, so the median is the last value of the stem 5 row: 59 kg.
range = 73 − 42 = 31 kg
53 occurs twice and 64 occurs twice, and no value occurs more often, so the data are bimodal with modes 53 kg and 64 kg.

questions.t: The five distinct numbers <var>p</var>, <var>q</var>, <var>r</var>, <var>s</var>, <var>t</var> are written in increasing order, so <var>p</var> is the smallest. Describe the effect on the median and on the mean of each change below. Treat each change separately, starting each time from the original five numbers.
p: <var>t</var> is increased by 20.
<var>p</var> is decreased by 15 and <var>t</var> is increased by 15.
<var>q</var> is increased by 4, and <var>q</var> is still less than <var>r</var>.
questions.al: The median of five ordered numbers is the third one, <var>r</var>.
ap: The order is unchanged and <var>r</var> is still third, so the median is unchanged. The sum increases by 20, so the mean increases by 20 ÷ 5 = 4.
The order is unchanged, so the median is unchanged. The sum changes by −15 + 15 = 0, so the mean is unchanged.
<var>q</var> stays in second place, so the median is still <var>r</var> and is unchanged. The sum increases by 4, so the mean increases by 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8.

questions.t: A set of four numbers has a mean of 30 and a median of 36.
p: Write down one such set of four numbers, and show that it has the required mean and median.
Prove that the smallest of the four numbers cannot be greater than 12.
questions.al: Let the four numbers in increasing order be <var>a</var> ≤ <var>b</var> ≤ <var>c</var> ≤ <var>d</var>. Mean 30 gives <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> + <var>c</var> + <var>d</var> = 120; median 36 gives <var>b</var> + <var>c</var> = 72; hence <var>a</var> + <var>d</var> = 48.
ap: Any four numbers satisfying <var>a</var> ≤ <var>b</var> ≤ <var>c</var> ≤ <var>d</var>, <var>b</var> + <var>c</var> = 72 and <var>a</var> + <var>d</var> = 48 is acceptable. For instance 11, 35, 37, 37: sum = 120 so the mean is 120 ÷ 4 = 30, and the median is (35 + 37) ÷ 2 = 36. Other valid answers include 8, 36, 36, 40 and 0, 30, 42, 48.

Since <var>b</var> ≤ <var>c</var> and <var>b</var> + <var>c</var> = 72, we get <var>c</var> ≥ 36. As <var>d</var> ≥ <var>c</var>, also <var>d</var> ≥ 36. Then <var>a</var> = 48 − <var>d</var> ≤ 48 − 36 = 12, so the smallest number is at most 12.

questions.t: A histogram shows the selling prices of the houses sold in one suburb during March. The columns, with prices in thousands of dollars, are: 300–399, 5 houses; 400–499, 18 houses; 500–599, 26 houses; 600–699, 14 houses; 700–799, 6 houses; 800–899, 3 houses; 900–999, 0 houses; 1000–1099, 2 houses.
p: How many houses were sold in the suburb during March?
What percentage of the houses sold for less than $600 000? Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
Which class contains the median selling price?
State whether the mean or the median selling price is the greater, and explain why.
ap: The median is in the (74 + 1) ÷ 2 = 37.5th position, i.e. the average of the 37th and 38th prices. Cumulative counts are 5, 23, 49, so both lie in the 500–599 class, that is, $500 000–$599 999.

The mean is the greater. The distribution is positively skewed: most houses are between $400 000 and $700 000, but a few sold for $800 000 or more, including two above $1 000 000. These few large values pull the mean up well above the median, which is unaffected by how extreme they are.

questions.t: A shop tallied the sizes of the T-shirts it sold in one week: S, 18; M, 24; L, 15; XL, 9; XXL, 4.
p: Determine the mode of the T-shirt sizes sold.
What percentage of the T-shirts sold were size S or size M?
Explain why calculating a mean T-shirt size makes no sense here.
Name the representation you would use to display this data, and give a reason.
ap: M has the highest frequency (24), so the mode is size M.
T-shirt size is categorical data, not numerical: S, M, L, XL and XXL are labels, not numbers, so they cannot be added or divided. Only the mode is meaningful for categorical data.

A column graph (a pictograph would also do), because the data are categorical with only five categories, so one column per size shows the comparison clearly. Histograms and stem-and-leaf plots are for numerical data.

questions.t: The population centre of a region is the point whose latitude is the average of the latitudes of all the people living there, and whose longitude is the average of their longitudes. Perth has latitude 32°S and longitude 116°E; Adelaide has latitude 35°S and longitude 139°E. Give all answers correct to 1 decimal place.
p: One person lives in Perth and one person lives in Adelaide. Find the latitude and the longitude of the population centre of these two people.
Find the latitude and the longitude of the population centre if 3 people live in Perth and 7 people live in Adelaide.

questions.t: Sydney has latitude 34°S, longitude 150°E and a population of 4 million; Melbourne has latitude 38°S, longitude 145°E and a population of 3 million; Brisbane has latitude 27°S, longitude 153°E and a population of 1 million. Find the latitude and the longitude of the population centre of the 8 million people living in these three cities, correct to 1 decimal place.

Every person in a small country lives in one of two towns. Alton has latitude 20°S and Bramble has latitude 32°S. The population centre of the country has latitude 24°S, and the two towns have a combined population of 6000 people. How many people live in each town?
questions.a: Let <var>a</var> people live in Alton and <var>b</var> in Bramble, so <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> = 6000. The average latitude is (20<var>a</var> + 32<var>b</var>) ÷ 6000 = 24, so 20<var>a</var> + 32<var>b</var> = 144 000. Also 20<var>a</var> + 20<var>b</var> = 20 × 6000 = 120 000. Subtracting gives 12<var>b</var> = 24 000, so <var>b</var> = 2000 and <var>a</var> = 4000. Alton has 4000 people and Bramble has 2000 people. (Check: (20 × 4000 + 32 × 2000) ÷ 6000 = (80 000 + 64 000) ÷ 6000 = 144 000 ÷ 6000 = 24.)

questions.t:
Take Sydney to be at latitude 34°S, longitude 150°E; Melbourne at 38°S, 145°E; and Perth at 32°S, 116°E. The populations of these three cities, in thousands, were:
1950 — Sydney 1557, Melbourne 1302, Perth 313
1990 — Sydney 3657, Melbourne 3081, Perth 1193
p: Find the latitude and the longitude of the population centre of the three cities in 1950, correct to 1 decimal place.
Do the same for 1990.
Describe the direction in which the population centre moved between 1950 and 1990, and explain why it moved that way.
ap: The latitude changed from 35.4°S to 35.3°S, a very small move north, while the longitude changed from 144.6°E to 142.9°E, a move of 1.7° to the west. So the centre moved west, and only slightly north. The main reason is that Perth grew fastest in relative terms: it held 313 ÷ 3172 ≈ 9.9% of the three-city population in 1950 but 1193 ÷ 7931 ≈ 15.0% in 1990. Because Perth is far to the west (116°E), giving it more weight drags the average longitude westwards.

questions.t: Answer both of the following, using full sentences.
p: Every person in a country lives in either Cato (latitude 40°S) or Dorne (latitude 25°S). Explain why the latitude of the country's population centre must always lie between 25°S and 40°S, no matter how the population is split between the two towns.
Give one reason why calculating Australia's population centre using only capital-city data is likely to give a misleading answer.
ap: If <var>c</var> people live in Cato and <var>d</var> in Dorne, the average latitude is (40<var>c</var> + 25<var>d</var>) ÷ (<var>c</var> + <var>d</var>), which can be written as 25 + 15<var>c</var> ÷ (<var>c</var> + <var>d</var>). Since <var>c</var> and <var>d</var> are both positive, the fraction <var>c</var> ÷ (<var>c</var> + <var>d</var>) lies strictly between 0 and 1, so the average latitude lies strictly between 25 + 0 = 25 and 25 + 15 = 40. It equals 25 only if nobody lives in Cato and 40 only if nobody lives in Dorne. (In words: a weighted average of two numbers always lies between them.)

Any one sound reason is acceptable, for example: a large share of Australians live outside the capital cities, in regional towns and rural areas, and leaving them out biases the centre towards the capitals; or the model treats everyone in a city as sitting at a single point, whereas cities spread over more than a degree of latitude and longitude; or the latitudes and longitudes are rounded to whole degrees, which introduces error of up to about 50 km.

questions.t: Convert between percentages, fractions and decimals.
p: Express 6.25% as a decimal.
Express 42% as a fraction in lowest terms.
Express 740 as a percentage.
Express 0.0035 as a percentage.
ap: 42100 = 2150
740 × 100% = 17.5%

questions.t: Evaluate each of the following.
p: What percentage is 36 cents of $8?
What percentage is 4.5 cm of 1.5 m?
ap: $8 = 800 cents, so 36800 × 100% = 4.5%
1.5 m = 150 cm, so 4.5150 × 100% = 3%

questions.t: Find the original quantity in each case.
p: 8% of an amount of money is $52.
A deposit of $684 is 18% of the full price of a lounge suite. Find the full price.
15% of a length is 42 cm.

questions.t: The Riverbend Auction House charges the vendor a commission of 7.5% of the selling price.
p: A carved chair was sold for $24 000. How much commission did the auction house receive, and how much was left for the vendor?
The auction house received a commission of $255 for selling a rug. What was the selling price of the rug, and how much did the vendor receive?
ap: Selling price = commission ÷ 0.075 = 255 ÷ 0.075 = $3400; vendor receives 3400 − 255 = $3145.

questions.t: Profits and losses here are always expressed as a percentage of the total costs.
p: A bakery's costs last year were $4 850 000 and it made a 3% profit on those costs. Find the profit and the total sales.
A hardware chain had costs of $2 184 000 and sales of $2 060 000. Find the loss and the percentage loss on costs, correct to two decimal places.
A courier company made a profit of $63 000, which was a 4.5% profit on its costs. Find the costs and the total sales.
ap: Loss = 2 184 000 − 2 060 000 = $124 000; percentage loss = 124 0002 184 000 × 100% ≈ 5.68%.

questions.t:
Income tax in the fictional nation of Calvaria is calculated as follows.
• There is no tax on the first $14 000 earned in a year.
• From $14 001 to $32 000, the rate is 16c for each dollar over $14 000.
• From $32 001 to $80 000, the rate is 26c for each dollar over $32 000.
• For incomes over $80 000, the rate is 38c for each dollar over $80 000.
p: Find the tax payable on a taxable income of $11 000.
Find the tax payable on a taxable income of $25 000.
Find the tax payable on a taxable income of $46 000.
Find the taxable income of a person whose tax was $9640.
ap: $11 000 is below $14 000, so the tax is $0.

$9640 is more than $2880 (the tax at $32 000) and less than $15 360 (the tax at $80 000), so the income is in the 26c band: 9640 − 2880 = $6760 of tax at 26c per dollar, so 6760 ÷ 0.26 = $26 000 above $32 000. Income = 32 000 + 26 000 = $58 000.

questions.t: Use the simple interest formula <var>I</var> = <var>PRT</var> for each part. Each part is a separate investment.
p: Find the simple interest earned on $14 500 invested for six years at 5.4% p.a.
Find the rate <var>R</var> if $15 000 earns $5400 simple interest over eight years.
Find the time <var>T</var> if $8400 earns $2352 simple interest at 7% p.a.
Find the principal <var>P</var> that earns $3186 simple interest at 5.9% p.a. over six years.
ap: 2352 = 8400 × 0.07 × <var>T</var> = 588<var>T</var>, so <var>T</var> = 4 years.

questions.t: The GST is 10% of the pre-tax price.
p: The pre-tax price of a bench saw is $1840. Find the after-tax price and the GST paid.
A plumbing job cost $572 after tax. Find the pre-tax price and the GST paid.
The GST charged on a repair was $37.50. Find the pre-tax price and the after-tax price.
ap: The GST is 10% of the pre-tax price, so pre-tax price = 37.50 ÷ 0.10 = $375; after-tax price = 375 + 37.50 = $412.50.

questions.t: Each part is a separate situation.
p: A club's membership rose from 480 to 618. Find the percentage increase.
After a 15% increase, an electricity bill is $977.50. What was the bill before the increase?
A koala population fell by 35% to 4160. What was the population before the fall?
A jacket is discounted by 45% and now sells for $87.45. Find the original price.
ap: 618480 × 100% = 128.75%, so the increase is 28.75%.
The new bill is 115% of the old, so old bill = 977.50 ÷ 1.15 = $850.
The new population is 65% of the old, so old population = 4160 ÷ 0.65 = 6400.
The sale price is 55% of the original, so original price = 87.45 ÷ 0.55 = $159.

questions.t: Coffee beans cost $18.50 per kilogram three years ago. In the three years since then the price rose by 8% in the first year, then by a further 12% in the second year, and then fell by 5% in the third year. Each percentage change applies to the price at the start of that year, not to the price three years ago.
p: Find the price per kilogram now, correct to the nearest cent.
Find the overall percentage change in the price over the three years, correct to two decimal places.
questions.al: The overall factor is 1.08 × 1.12 × 0.95 = 1.149 12.
ap: 1.149 12 = 114.912% of the original price, so the price has increased by 14.91% (correct to two decimal places).

questions.t: Council rates in Marrowfield Shire have risen by 4.5% every year for the last eight years.
p: By what percentage have the rates risen over the whole eight-year period? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
The rates on one property are now $2320. What were the rates on that property eight years ago, correct to the nearest cent?
questions.al: Each year the rates are 104.5% of the previous year's rates, so the eight-year factor is (1.045)<sup>8</sup> ≈ 1.422 101.
ap: 1.422 101 = 142.2101% of the original, so the rise is 42.21% (correct to two decimal places).

questions.t: Freya invests $24 000 for seven years at 6.4% p.a., compounded annually. Use A<sub><var>n</var></sub> = <var>P</var>(1 + <var>R</var>)<sup><var>n</var></sup>.
p: Find the value of the investment at the end of the seven years, correct to the nearest cent.
Find the total compound interest earned over the seven years.
Find the simple interest that $24 000 would have earned over seven years at the same rate of 6.4% p.a.
How much more interest does the compound interest investment earn?

questions.t: In each part the interest is compounded monthly at the rate given per month.
p: Kwame invests $18 000 at 0.45% per month for five years. Find the value of the investment at the end of the five years, correct to the nearest cent.
Lena wants an investment to be worth $75 000 in eight years' time. The rate is 0.6% per month. How much must she invest now, correct to the nearest cent?
ap: The time is 96 months and <var>R</var> = 0.006, so 75 000 = <var>P</var> × (1.006)<sup>96</sup> = <var>P</var> × 1.775 849…, giving <var>P</var> = 75 000 ÷ (1.006)<sup>96</sup> ≈ $42 233.31.

questions.t: A delivery van was bought for $58 000 and depreciates at 18% p.a. Use A<sub><var>n</var></sub> = <var>P</var>(1 − <var>R</var>)<sup><var>n</var></sup>.
p: Find the value of the van after five years, correct to the nearest cent.
Find the total percentage decrease in value over the five years, correct to two decimal places.
Find the average reduction in value, in dollars per year, over the five years, correct to the nearest cent.
questions.al: Here 1 − <var>R</var> = 0.82.
ap: The final value is 37.073 984% of the original, so the decrease is 100% − 37.07% = 62.93% (correct to two decimal places).
Total depreciation = 58 000 − 21 502.91 = $36 497.09, so the average reduction is 36 497.09 ÷ 5 ≈ $7299.42 per year.

questions.t: Nadia bought a share portfolio for $45 000. For the first three years the portfolio grew in value by 7% each year; for the next three years it fell in value by 7% each year.
p: Find the value of the portfolio at the end of the six years, correct to the nearest dollar.
Find the equivalent simple interest rate of change in value per year over the six years, correct to two decimal places, and state whether it is a gain or a loss.
ap: The change in value is 44 341.74 − 45 000 = −$658.26. As a simple interest rate, I = PRT gives R = 658.2645 000 × 6 = 0.002 438, so the equivalent rate is 0.24% per year, and it is a loss. (Note that a 7% rise followed by a 7% fall does not cancel: 1.07 × 0.93 = 0.9951.)

questions.t:
Two banks offer these fixed investment packages, with interest compounded annually and no withdrawals during the term.
Bank Rivera: 6.2% p.a., fixed for five years.
Bank Solano: 4.8% p.a., fixed for seven years.
p: Find the percentage growth of each package over its whole term, correct to two decimal places, and say which package gives the greater growth.

A customer invests $12 000 with Bank Rivera for its full five years. How much would she need to invest with Bank Solano, for its full seven years, to finish with the same final amount? Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
ap: Rivera: (1.062)<sup>5</sup> ≈ 1.350 898, a growth of 35.09%. Solano: (1.048)<sup>7</sup> ≈ 1.388 446, a growth of 38.84%. Bank Solano gives the greater growth, even though its annual rate is lower, because the term is two years longer.

questions.t: The length of a rectangle is decreased by 15% and its width is increased by 24%.
p: Find the percentage change in the area of the rectangle, and state whether it is an increase or a decrease.

The length is now left unchanged, and the width is changed once more so that the area returns to exactly its original value. Find the percentage change in the width in this final step, correct to two decimal places, and state whether it is an increase or a decrease.
questions.al: Let the original length be <var>L</var> and the original width be <var>W</var>, so the original area is <var>LW</var>.
ap: New area = (0.85<var>L</var>) × (1.24<var>W</var>) = 1.054<var>LW</var>, which is 105.4% of <var>LW</var>, so the area increases by 5.4%.

The width must be multiplied by a factor k with 1.054k = 1, so k = 11.054 = 0.948 766 6…, which is 94.8767% of the current width. So the width must be decreased by 5.12% (correct to two decimal places). Note that this is not 5.4%, because the decrease is measured against the already-increased width.

questions.t: In the town of Kellerton in 2024, 15% of the adults cycled to work and the other 85% did not. During 2025, 12% of those who cycled to work stopped cycling to work, and 8% of those who did not cycle to work started cycling to work. No adults moved into or out of the town, and the total number of adults did not change.
p: What percentage of the adults cycled to work at the end of 2025?
By what percentage did the number of adults cycling to work increase during 2025? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
ap: Of the 15% who cycled, 88% still cycle: 15% × 0.88 = 13.2% of the adults. Of the 85% who did not cycle, 8% now cycle: 85% × 0.08 = 6.8% of the adults. Total = 13.2% + 6.8% = 20% of the adults.
2015 × 100% = 133.333…%, so the number of cyclists increased by 33.33% (correct to two decimal places).

questions.t: A beaker holds 500 mL of pure cordial. The following step is then carried out 12 times in all: 100 mL of water is stirred thoroughly into the beaker, making 600 mL of mixture, and then 100 mL of the mixture is poured away, leaving 500 mL in the beaker.
p: What fraction of the cordial present at the start of a step is still in the beaker at the end of that step? Explain your reasoning.
What percentage of the original cordial is in the beaker after all 12 steps? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
ap: After the water is stirred in, all of the cordial is spread evenly through 600 mL of mixture. Pouring away 100 mL removes 100600 = ⅙ of the mixture, and therefore ⅙ of the cordial, so ⅚ of the cordial remains. (Adding water does not change how much cordial is present; only pouring away does.)
Each step multiplies the amount of cordial by ⅚, so after 12 steps the fraction remaining is (⅚)12 = 244 140 6252 176 782 336 ≈ 0.112 157. So about 11.22% of the original cordial remains.

questions.t: Diego buys a warehouse, and immediately spends a further amount equal to 8% of the purchase price on repairs. He borrows the whole amount he has spent (purchase price plus repairs) at 6% p.a. compound interest and makes no repayments. Exactly three years later he sells the warehouse for $618 000 and repays the loan in full. His profit — the selling price minus the amount he repays — is exactly 15% of the total amount he spent.
p: Taking the purchase price of the warehouse to be $<var>x</var>, write down an equation in <var>x</var>.
Find the purchase price of the warehouse, correct to the nearest dollar.
ap: The total spent is <var>x</var> + 0.08<var>x</var> = 1.08<var>x</var>. After three years the amount owing is 1.08<var>x</var> × (1.06)<sup>3</sup>, and the profit is 618 000 − 1.08<var>x</var> × (1.06)<sup>3</sup>. So the equation is 618 000 − 1.08<var>x</var>(1.06)<sup>3</sup> = 0.15 × 1.08<var>x</var>.

questions.t: A rectangle has length (5 + 2√3) cm and width (5 − 2√3) cm. Give each answer in simplest exact form.

32√3 − 3 − 32√3 + 3

questions.t: In this question <var>a</var> and <var>b</var> are positive numbers.
p: Show that (√<var>a</var> + √<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> = <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> + 2√(<var>ab</var>), and that (√<var>a</var> − √<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> = <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> − 2√(<var>ab</var>).
Use part a to write √(14 + 6√5) in the form <var>p</var> + <var>q</var>√5, where <var>p</var> and <var>q</var> are positive integers.
Use part a to write √(11 − 4√7) in the form √<var>m</var> − <var>n</var>, where <var>m</var> and <var>n</var> are positive integers.
ap: (√<var>a</var> + √<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> = (√<var>a</var>)<sup>2</sup> + 2√<var>a</var> × √<var>b</var> + (√<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> = <var>a</var> + 2√(<var>ab</var>) + <var>b</var>, using √<var>a</var> × √<var>b</var> = √(<var>ab</var>). Replacing √<var>b</var> by −√<var>b</var> only changes the sign of the middle term, giving (√<var>a</var> − √<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> = <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> − 2√(<var>ab</var>).

Write 6√5 = 2 × 3√5 = 2√45, so we need <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> = 14 and <var>ab</var> = 45. These give <var>a</var> = 9, <var>b</var> = 5, so 14 + 6√5 = (3 + √5)<sup>2</sup>. Since 3 + √5 > 0, √(14 + 6√5) = 3 + √5, i.e. <var>p</var> = 3 and <var>q</var> = 1. Check: (3 + √5)<sup>2</sup> = 9 + 6√5 + 5 = 14 + 6√5.

Write 4√7 = 2 × 2√7 = 2√28, so we need <var>a</var> + <var>b</var> = 11 and <var>ab</var> = 28, giving <var>a</var> = 7, <var>b</var> = 4. Hence 11 − 4√7 = (√7 − 2)<sup>2</sup>, and √7 − 2 > 0, so √(11 − 4√7) = √7 − 2, i.e. <var>m</var> = 7 and <var>n</var> = 2. Check: (√7 − 2)<sup>2</sup> = 7 − 4√7 + 4 = 11 − 4√7.

questions.t: Express 11 + √2 + √3 + √6 with a rational denominator. Hint: factorise the denominator by grouping.
questions.a: Group the denominator: 1 + √2 + √3 + √6 = (1 + √2) + √3(1 + √2) = (1 + √2)(1 + √3), since √3 × √2 = √6. So the expression is 1(1 + √2)(1 + √3). Rationalise each bracket in turn: multiply top and bottom by (√2 − 1)(√3 − 1), and use (√2 + 1)(√2 − 1) = 1 and (√3 + 1)(√3 − 1) = 2. This gives (√2 − 1)(√3 − 1)1 × 2 = √6 − √2 − √3 + 12. (Check numerically: the denominator is about 6.5958 and 1 ÷ 6.5958 ≈ 0.1516, while (2.4495 − 1.4142 − 1.7321 + 1) ÷ 2 ≈ 0.1516.)

questions.t: Let <var>n</var> be a positive integer.
p: Show that 1√n + √(n + 2) = √(n + 2) − √n2.

Hence find the exact value of 11 + √3 + 1√3 + √5 + 1√5 + √7 + ... + 1√23 + 5, in which the numbers under the square root signs run through the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, ..., 25 (so the first denominator is √1 + √3 and the last is √23 + √25).
ap: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate √(n + 2) − √n. The denominator becomes (√(n + 2) + √n)(√(n + 2) − √n) = (n + 2) − n = 2, so the fraction equals √(n + 2) − √n2.

By part a, each term equals ½(√(<var>n</var> + 2) − √<var>n</var>), so the sum is ½[(√3 − √1) + (√5 − √3) + (√7 − √5) + ... + (√25 − √23)]. Every surd cancels with the next one except −√1 and +√25, leaving ½(√25 − √1) = ½(5 − 1) = 2. (There are 12 terms, for <var>n</var> = 1, 3, 5, ..., 23.)

questions.t: Let <var>x</var> = 2 + √3.
p: Show that x + 1x = 4.
Hence find the value of x2 + 1x2.
Hence find the value of x3 + 1x3.
ap: 1x = 12 + √3 = 2 − √3(2 + √3)(2 − √3) = 2 − √34 − 3 = 2 − √3. Hence x + 1x = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3) = 4.
Squaring part a: (x + 1x)2 = x2 + 2 + 1x2, so x2 + 1x2 = 42 − 2 = 14.
Cubing part a: (x + 1x)3 = x3 + 3x + 3x + 1x3 = x3 + 1x3 + 3(x + 1x). So x3 + 1x3 = 43 − 3 × 4 = 64 − 12 = 52. (Check: (2 + √3)3 ≈ 51.9808 and (2 − √3)3 ≈ 0.0192, and these sum to 52.)
