multiplying through by 20 gives 5<var>x</var> + 8<var>x</var> = 26, so 13<var>x</var> = 26 and <var>x</var> = 2.
multiplying through by 15 gives 5(x − 1) − 3(x − 4) = 4, so 2x + 7 = 4 and x = −32.

questions.t: Simplify each expression. State each answer in factorised form.
p: x2 + 3x − 28x2 − 16
2x2 + 5x − 3x2 + 6x + 9 × x2 + 2x − 32x2 − 5x + 2
3x − 2 − 4x2 + x − 6
ap: (x + 7)(x − 4)(x − 4)(x + 4) = x + 7x + 4.
the four factorisations are (2x − 1)(x + 3), (x + 3)2, (x + 3)(x − 1) and (2x − 1)(x − 2), so the product is (2x − 1)(x + 3)(x + 3)(x − 1)(x + 3)2(2x − 1)(x − 2) = x − 1x − 2.
x2 + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2), so the expression is 3(x + 3) − 4(x + 3)(x − 2) = 3x + 5(x + 3)(x − 2).

questions.t: A laboratory has 250 mL of a solution that is 12% acid by volume. How many millilitres of pure (100%) acid must be added so that the new solution is 20% acid by volume? Check your answer.
questions.a: Let <var>x</var> mL of pure acid be added. The acid present at the start is 12% of 250 = 30 mL, so the new solution contains (30 + <var>x</var>) mL of acid in a total volume of (250 + <var>x</var>) mL. Then 30 + <var>x</var> = 0.2(250 + <var>x</var>) = 50 + 0.2<var>x</var>, so 0.8<var>x</var> = 20 and <var>x</var> = 25. So 25 mL of pure acid must be added. Check: the new solution holds 55 mL of acid in 275 mL, and 55 ÷ 275 = 0.2 = 20%.

questions.t: Factorise each expression completely.
p: (4<var>x</var> + 5<var>y</var>)<sup>2</sup> − (<var>x</var> − 3<var>y</var>)<sup>2</sup>
18<var>x</var><sup>4</sup><var>y</var> − 3<var>x</var><sup>3</sup><var>y</var> − 45<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var>
ap: using <var>A</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>B</var><sup>2</sup> = (<var>A</var> − <var>B</var>)(<var>A</var> + <var>B</var>) with <var>A</var> = 4<var>x</var> + 5<var>y</var> and <var>B</var> = <var>x</var> − 3<var>y</var>: <var>A</var> − <var>B</var> = 3<var>x</var> + 8<var>y</var> and <var>A</var> + <var>B</var> = 5<var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var>, so the factorisation is (3<var>x</var> + 8<var>y</var>)(5<var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var>). (Check by expanding: 15<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 46<var>xy</var> + 16<var>y</var><sup>2</sup>.)

take out 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var>: 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var>(6<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>x</var> − 15). For 6<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>x</var> − 15, <var>ac</var> = −90 and −10 + 9 = −1, so 6<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 10<var>x</var> + 9<var>x</var> − 15 = 2<var>x</var>(3<var>x</var> − 5) + 3(3<var>x</var> − 5) = (3<var>x</var> − 5)(2<var>x</var> + 3). Hence the answer is 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var>(3<var>x</var> − 5)(2<var>x</var> + 3).

questions.t: Factorise each expression completely. In each part, group the terms so that a difference of two squares appears.
p: <var>a</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>ab</var> + 9<var>b</var><sup>2</sup> − 25<var>c</var><sup>2</sup>
4<var>p</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>q</var><sup>2</sup> + 10<var>qr</var> − 25<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>

9<var>a</var><sup>2</sup><var>m</var><sup>2</sup> − 25<var>b</var><sup>2</sup><var>m</var><sup>2</sup> − 9<var>a</var><sup>2</sup><var>n</var><sup>2</sup> + 25<var>b</var><sup>2</sup><var>n</var><sup>2</sup>
ap: the first three terms are (<var>a</var> − 3<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup>, so the expression is (<var>a</var> − 3<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> − (5<var>c</var>)<sup>2</sup> = (<var>a</var> − 3<var>b</var> − 5<var>c</var>)(<var>a</var> − 3<var>b</var> + 5<var>c</var>).

take −1 out of the last three terms: 4<var>p</var><sup>2</sup> − (<var>q</var><sup>2</sup> − 10<var>qr</var> + 25<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>) = (2<var>p</var>)<sup>2</sup> − (<var>q</var> − 5<var>r</var>)<sup>2</sup> = (2<var>p</var> − <var>q</var> + 5<var>r</var>)(2<var>p</var> + <var>q</var> − 5<var>r</var>).

group in pairs: <var>m</var><sup>2</sup>(9<var>a</var><sup>2</sup> − 25<var>b</var><sup>2</sup>) − <var>n</var><sup>2</sup>(9<var>a</var><sup>2</sup> − 25<var>b</var><sup>2</sup>) = (9<var>a</var><sup>2</sup> − 25<var>b</var><sup>2</sup>)(<var>m</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>n</var><sup>2</sup>) = (3<var>a</var> − 5<var>b</var>)(3<var>a</var> + 5<var>b</var>)(<var>m</var> − <var>n</var>)(<var>m</var> + <var>n</var>).

questions.t: Expand and collect like terms.
p: (2<var>a</var> − <var>b</var> + 3<var>c</var>)<sup>2</sup>
(2<var>x</var> + 3<var>y</var>)(4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>xy</var> + 9<var>y</var><sup>2</sup>)
ap: squaring a sum of three terms gives the three squares plus twice each of the three products: (2<var>a</var>)<sup>2</sup> + (−<var>b</var>)<sup>2</sup> + (3<var>c</var>)<sup>2</sup> + 2(2<var>a</var>)(−<var>b</var>) + 2(2<var>a</var>)(3<var>c</var>) + 2(−<var>b</var>)(3<var>c</var>) = 4<var>a</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>b</var><sup>2</sup> + 9<var>c</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>ab</var> + 12<var>ac</var> − 6<var>bc</var>.

2<var>x</var>(4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>xy</var> + 9<var>y</var><sup>2</sup>) + 3<var>y</var>(4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>xy</var> + 9<var>y</var><sup>2</sup>) = 8<var>x</var><sup>3</sup> − 12<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var> + 18<var>xy</var><sup>2</sup> + 12<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var> − 18<var>xy</var><sup>2</sup> + 27<var>y</var><sup>3</sup> = 8<var>x</var><sup>3</sup> + 27<var>y</var><sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: Solve the equation 23(x − 1) − 34(x − 2) = 16(x + 3) − 512, and check your solution by substituting it back into both sides.
questions.a: Multiply both sides by 12, the lowest common denominator: 8(x − 1) − 9(x − 2) = 2(x + 3) − 5. Expanding, 8x − 8 − 9x + 18 = 2x + 6 − 5, so −x + 10 = 2x + 1. Hence 9 = 3x and x = 3. Check: LHS = 23 × 2 − 34 × 1 = 43 − 34 = 712; RHS = 16 × 6 − 512 = 1 − 512 = 712. ∴ x = 3.

questions.t: Each part below describes a different rectangular room.
p: The width of the room is three-quarters of its length. If the width were 2 m more and the length 2 m less, the room would be square. Find the length and the width of the room.
The length of the room is 4 m more than its width. If the length were increased by 2 m and the width decreased by 1 m, the area would be unchanged. Find the length and the width of the room.
ap: Let the length be L m, so the width is 34L m. The altered room is square, so 34L + 2 = L − 2, giving 4 = 14L and L = 16. The length is 16 m and the width is 12 m. (Check: 12 + 2 = 14 and 16 − 2 = 14.)

Let the width be <var>w</var> m, so the length is (<var>w</var> + 4) m and the area is <var>w</var>(<var>w</var> + 4) m<sup>2</sup>. The altered room measures (<var>w</var> + 6) m by (<var>w</var> − 1) m, so (<var>w</var> + 6)(<var>w</var> − 1) = <var>w</var>(<var>w</var> + 4). Expanding, <var>w</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>w</var> − 6 = <var>w</var><sup>2</sup> + 4<var>w</var>, so <var>w</var> = 6. The width is 6 m and the length is 10 m. (Check: 10 × 6 = 60 and 12 × 5 = 60.)

questions.t: Priya is <var>c</var> km due south of Raj on a long straight north–south road. At the same instant they both start walking due north along that road, Priya at a constant <var>p</var> km/h and Raj at a constant <var>q</var> km/h, where <var>p</var> > <var>q</var>. Find, in terms of <var>c</var>, <var>p</var> and <var>q</var>, the distance Priya has walked at the moment she catches up with Raj.
questions.a: Let t hours be the time until Priya catches Raj. In that time Priya walks pt km and Raj walks qt km, and Priya must cover Raj's distance plus the initial gap of c km, so pt = qt + c. Hence t(p − q) = c and t = cp − q hours, which is positive because p > q. The distance Priya has walked is pt = pcp − q km.

questions.t: The points <var>P</var>(−3, 2) and <var>Q</var>(5, 8) are plotted on the number plane.
p: Find the distance <var>PQ</var>.
Find the coordinates of the midpoint of the interval <var>PQ</var>.

questions.t: Find the gradient of:
p: the interval <var>AB</var>, where <var>A</var> is (−2, 7) and <var>B</var> is (4, −5)
the interval <var>CD</var>, where <var>C</var> is (3, −4) and <var>D</var> is (−1, −4)
any line perpendicular to a line of gradient 35
ap: (−4 − (−4)) ÷ (−1 − 3) = 0 ÷ (−4) = 0; the interval is horizontal.
−53, because 35 × (−53) = −1.

questions.t: This question is about the gradient-intercept form <var>y</var> = <var>mx</var> + <var>b</var>.
p: Write down the equation of the line with gradient −4 and <var>y</var>-intercept 7.
State the gradient and the <var>y</var>-intercept of the line 3<var>x</var> + 5<var>y</var> − 20 = 0.
ap: <var>y</var> = −4<var>x</var> + 7.
5y = −3x + 20, so y = −35x + 4. The gradient is −35 and the y-intercept is 4.

questions.t: Find the coordinates of the <var>x</var>-intercept and of the <var>y</var>-intercept of the line 4<var>x</var> − 7<var>y</var> = 28.
questions.a: Put <var>y</var> = 0: 4<var>x</var> = 28, so <var>x</var> = 7 and the <var>x</var>-intercept is (7, 0). Put <var>x</var> = 0: −7<var>y</var> = 28, so <var>y</var> = −4 and the <var>y</var>-intercept is (0, −4).

questions.t: Express y = −35x + 27 in the general form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are integers.
questions.a: Multiply both sides by 35: 35<var>y</var> = −21<var>x</var> + 10, so 21<var>x</var> + 35<var>y</var> − 10 = 0. Any non-zero multiple of this equation, such as 42<var>x</var> + 70<var>y</var> − 20 = 0, is equally correct.

questions.t: Find the equation of each line below. Give each answer in gradient-intercept form or in general form.
p: The line with gradient −3 that passes through the point (2, −5).
The line that passes through the two points (−4, 1) and (6, −3).
ap: <var>y</var> − (−5) = −3(<var>x</var> − 2) gives <var>y</var> + 5 = −3<var>x</var> + 6, so <var>y</var> = −3<var>x</var> + 1. Check: −3 × 2 + 1 = −5.
Gradient = (−3 − 1) ÷ (6 − (−4)) = −4 ÷ 10 = −25. Then y − 1 = −25(x + 4), so 5y − 5 = −2x − 8, giving 2x + 5y + 3 = 0, or y = −25x − 35. Check (6, −3): 12 − 15 + 3 = 0.

questions.t: Find the equation of each line described below.
p: The line parallel to <var>y</var> = 4<var>x</var> − 9 that passes through the point (−1, 6).
The line perpendicular to 2<var>x</var> + 3<var>y</var> = 12 that passes through the point (4, −1).
ap: Parallel lines have equal gradients, so the gradient is 4: <var>y</var> − 6 = 4(<var>x</var> + 1), giving <var>y</var> = 4<var>x</var> + 10. Check: 4 × (−1) + 10 = 6.

2x + 3y = 12 is y = −23x + 4, so its gradient is −23 and the perpendicular gradient is 32. Then y + 1 = 32(x − 4), so 2y + 2 = 3x − 12, giving 3x − 2y − 14 = 0, or y = 32x − 7. Check (4, −1): 12 + 2 − 14 = 0.

questions.t: Solve each pair of simultaneous equations by elimination.
p: 3<var>x</var> + 4<var>y</var> = 10 and 5<var>x</var> − 2<var>y</var> = 8
4<var>x</var> − 3<var>y</var> = 18 and 5<var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var> = 11
ap: 2 × (second): 10<var>x</var> − 4<var>y</var> = 16. Adding this to 3<var>x</var> + 4<var>y</var> = 10 gives 13<var>x</var> = 26, so <var>x</var> = 2; then 6 + 4<var>y</var> = 10, so <var>y</var> = 1. Solution <var>x</var> = 2, <var>y</var> = 1. Check: 5(2) − 2(1) = 8.

2 × (first): 8<var>x</var> − 6<var>y</var> = 36; 3 × (second): 15<var>x</var> + 6<var>y</var> = 33. Adding: 23<var>x</var> = 69, so <var>x</var> = 3; then 12 − 3<var>y</var> = 18, so −3<var>y</var> = 6 and <var>y</var> = −2. Solution <var>x</var> = 3, <var>y</var> = −2. Check: 5(3) + 2(−2) = 11.

questions.t: Solve the simultaneous equations <var>y</var> = 2<var>x</var> − 7 and 3<var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var> = 7 by substitution, and state the coordinates of the point where the two lines meet.
questions.a: 3<var>x</var> + 2(2<var>x</var> − 7) = 7, so 7<var>x</var> − 14 = 7, 7<var>x</var> = 21 and <var>x</var> = 3. Then <var>y</var> = 2(3) − 7 = −1. The lines meet at (3, −1). Check: 3(3) + 2(−1) = 7.

questions.t: Use gradients to answer each part.
p: The line through (−2, 5) and (4, k) has gradient −12. Find the value of k.
The points <var>A</var>(1, −3), <var>B</var>(4, 3) and <var>C</var>(<var>t</var>, 9) are collinear. Find the value of <var>t</var>.
ap: (k − 5) ÷ (4 − (−2)) = −12, so k − 5 = 6 × (−12) = −3 and k = 2.

Gradient <var>AB</var> = (3 − (−3)) ÷ (4 − 1) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. For <var>C</var> to lie on the same line, gradient <var>BC</var> = 2, so (9 − 3) ÷ (<var>t</var> − 4) = 2, giving 6 = 2<var>t</var> − 8 and <var>t</var> = 7. Check: from <var>A</var>(1, −3) to <var>C</var>(7, 9) the gradient is 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

questions.t: The points <var>P</var>(−1, 2), <var>Q</var>(3, 4) and <var>R</var>(5, 0) are the vertices of a triangle.
p: Find the exact lengths <var>PQ</var>, <var>QR</var> and <var>PR</var>, writing each surd in simplest form.
Show that △<var>PQR</var> is right-angled and state which vertex the right angle is at.
ap: <var>PQ</var><sup>2</sup> = 4<sup>2</sup> + 2<sup>2</sup> = 20, so <var>PQ</var> = 2√5. <var>QR</var><sup>2</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> + (−4)<sup>2</sup> = 20, so <var>QR</var> = 2√5. <var>PR</var><sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> + (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 40, so <var>PR</var> = 2√10.

PQ2 + QR2 = 20 + 20 = 40 = PR2, so by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem the right angle is at Q. (Equivalently, gradient PQ = 24 = 12 and gradient QR = −4 ÷ 2 = −2, and 12 × (−2) = −1.) The triangle is also isosceles, since PQ = QR = 2√5.

questions.t: <var>A</var> is the point (−2, 1) and <var>B</var> is the point (6, 7).
p: Find the coordinates of the midpoint <var>M</var> of the interval <var>AB</var>.
Find the gradient of the line <var>AB</var>.
Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of <var>AB</var>, giving it in general form.
ap: (7 − 1) ÷ (6 − (−2)) = 68 = 34.
The perpendicular bisector passes through M(2, 4) with gradient −43: y − 4 = −43(x − 2), so 3y − 12 = −4x + 8, giving 4x + 3y − 20 = 0. Check M: 8 + 12 − 20 = 0.

questions.t: At a school fete, sausage rolls are all sold at one price and fruit smoothies are all sold at another price. Four sausage rolls and three smoothies cost $16.50 altogether, while six sausage rolls and five smoothies cost $26.50 altogether. By introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations, find the price of one sausage roll and the price of one smoothie.
questions.a: Let <var>r</var> be the price of a sausage roll and <var>s</var> the price of a smoothie, both in dollars. Then 4<var>r</var> + 3<var>s</var> = 16.50 … (1) and 6<var>r</var> + 5<var>s</var> = 26.50 … (2). 5 × (1): 20<var>r</var> + 15<var>s</var> = 82.50; 3 × (2): 18<var>r</var> + 15<var>s</var> = 79.50. Subtracting gives 2<var>r</var> = 3, so <var>r</var> = 1.50. Substituting into (1): 6 + 3<var>s</var> = 16.50, so 3<var>s</var> = 10.50 and <var>s</var> = 3.50. A sausage roll costs $1.50 and a smoothie costs $3.50. Check in (2): 6(1.50) + 5(3.50) = 9 + 17.50 = 26.50.

questions.t: <var>A</var> is the point (−3, 1) and <var>B</var> is the point (9, 7).
p: Find the coordinates of the point <var>P</var> on the interval <var>AB</var> for which <var>AP</var> : <var>PB</var> = 2 : 1.
Find the equation of the line that passes through <var>P</var> and is perpendicular to <var>AB</var>.
ap: From A to B the run is 9 − (−3) = 12 and the rise is 7 − 1 = 6. Since AP : PB = 2 : 1, P is 23 of the way from A to B, so P = (−3 + 23 × 12, 1 + 23 × 6) = (5, 5). Check: AP = √(82 + 42) = √80 = 4√5 and PB = √(42 + 22) = √20 = 2√5, so AP : PB = 2 : 1.
Gradient AB = 6 ÷ 12 = 12, so the perpendicular gradient is −2. Through (5, 5): y − 5 = −2(x − 5), so y = −2x + 15, that is 2x + y − 15 = 0.

questions.t: △<var>ABC</var> has vertices <var>A</var>(2, 2), <var>B</var>(4, 12) and <var>C</var>(12, 4). A median of a triangle is the interval joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.
p: Find the equation of the median from <var>A</var> and the equation of the median from <var>B</var>.
Find the coordinates of the point <var>X</var> where these two medians meet.
Show that the median from <var>C</var> also passes through <var>X</var>.
ap: Midpoint of <var>BC</var> = ((4 + 12) ÷ 2, (12 + 4) ÷ 2) = (8, 8). Gradient from <var>A</var>(2, 2) to (8, 8) is 6 ÷ 6 = 1, so the median from <var>A</var> is <var>y</var> − 2 = 1(<var>x</var> − 2), that is <var>y</var> = <var>x</var>. Midpoint of <var>AC</var> = (7, 3). Gradient from <var>B</var>(4, 12) to (7, 3) is (3 − 12) ÷ (7 − 4) = −3, so the median from <var>B</var> is <var>y</var> − 12 = −3(<var>x</var> − 4), that is <var>y</var> = −3<var>x</var> + 24.

Solving <var>y</var> = <var>x</var> with <var>y</var> = −3<var>x</var> + 24: <var>x</var> = −3<var>x</var> + 24, so 4<var>x</var> = 24, <var>x</var> = 6 and <var>y</var> = 6. Hence <var>X</var> is (6, 6).

Midpoint of AB = (3, 7). Gradient from C(12, 4) to (3, 7) is (7 − 4) ÷ (3 − 12) = −13, so the median from C is y − 4 = −13(x − 12), that is y = −13x + 8. When x = 6, y = −2 + 8 = 6, so (6, 6) lies on this median too. All three medians pass through X(6, 6), which is the point (2 + 4 + 123, 2 + 12 + 43).

questions.t: <var>M</var> is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin <var>O</var> to the line 3<var>x</var> + 4<var>y</var> − 25 = 0.
p: Find the equation of the line <var>OM</var>.
Find the coordinates of <var>M</var>.
Find the length <var>OM</var>, which is the shortest distance from the origin to the line.
ap: 3x + 4y − 25 = 0 rearranges to y = −34x + 254, so its gradient is −34 and the perpendicular gradient is 43. The line OM passes through the origin, so OM is y = 43x, that is 4x − 3y = 0.
Substituting y = 43x into 3x + 4y = 25 gives 3x + 163x = 25, so 253x = 25, x = 3 and y = 4. Hence M is (3, 4). Check: 3(3) + 4(4) − 25 = 0.

questions.t: <var>OABC</var> is a rhombus whose vertices, taken in order, are <var>O</var>(0, 0), <var>A</var>(<var>a</var>, <var>b</var>), <var>B</var>(<var>a</var> + <var>c</var>, <var>b</var>) and <var>C</var>(<var>c</var>, 0), where <var>a</var>, <var>b</var> and <var>c</var> are positive numbers and <var>a</var> ≠ <var>c</var>. Its diagonals are <var>OB</var> and <var>AC</var>.
p: Write down the gradient of <var>OB</var> and the gradient of <var>AC</var>.
Show that (gradient of OB) × (gradient of AC) = b2a2 − c2.
Use the fact that <var>OA</var> = <var>OC</var> to show that <var>a</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>b</var><sup>2</sup> = <var>c</var><sup>2</sup>, and hence that <var>OB</var> ⊥ <var>AC</var>.
ap: Gradient of OB = b − 0(a + c) − 0 = ba + c. Gradient of AC = 0 − bc − a = ba − c.
Their product is ba + c × ba − c = b2(a + c)(a − c) = b2a2 − c2.

OA = √(a2 + b2) and OC = c. All sides of a rhombus are equal, so OA = OC, giving a2 + b2 = c2. Therefore a2 − c2 = −b2, and the product of the gradients from part b is b2−b2 = −1. Since b > 0 and a ≠ c, neither diagonal is vertical, so a product of −1 means OB ⊥ AC: the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular.

questions.t: Show that the three lines 2<var>x</var> − <var>y</var> = 3, <var>x</var> + 2<var>y</var> = 4 and 3<var>x</var> + <var>y</var> = 7 are concurrent; that is, show that all three pass through a single point.
questions.a: The gradients of the three lines are 2, −12 and −3, so no two of them are parallel and each pair meets exactly once. From 2x − y = 3 we get y = 2x − 3. Substituting into x + 2y = 4: x + 2(2x − 3) = 4, so 5x − 6 = 4, 5x = 10, x = 2 and y = 1. So the first two lines meet only at (2, 1). Substituting (2, 1) into the third equation: 3(2) + 1 = 7, which is true, so (2, 1) lies on the third line as well. Hence all three lines pass through (2, 1) and they are concurrent.

questions.t: Solve each equation.
p: <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 4) = 0
(<var>x</var> − 5)(<var>x</var> + 2) = 0
3<var>x</var>(2<var>x</var> − 7) = 0
ap: <var>x</var> = 0 or <var>x</var> = −4.
<var>x</var> = 5 or <var>x</var> = −2.
x = 0 or 2x − 7 = 0, so x = 0 or x = 72.

questions.t: Solve each quadratic equation by factorising. (Never divide by <var>x</var> — always factorise.)
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 7<var>x</var> = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> = 11<var>x</var>
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 49 = 0
ap: <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> − 7) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 0 or <var>x</var> = 7.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>x</var> = 0, so <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> − 11) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 0 or <var>x</var> = 11.
(<var>x</var> − 7)(<var>x</var> + 7) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 7 or <var>x</var> = −7.

questions.t: Solve each quadratic equation by factorising.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 10<var>x</var> + 21 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 9<var>x</var> + 20 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var> − 35 = 0
ap: (<var>x</var> + 3)(<var>x</var> + 7) = 0, so <var>x</var> = −3 or <var>x</var> = −7.
(<var>x</var> − 4)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 4 or <var>x</var> = 5.
(<var>x</var> + 7)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0, so <var>x</var> = −7 or <var>x</var> = 5.

questions.t: Solve each equation if possible. If an equation has no solution, say so and explain why.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 25 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 3<var>x</var> = 40
5<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 10<var>x</var> − 75 = 0
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> = −25, and the square of a real number is never negative, so there is no solution.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 3<var>x</var> − 40 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 8)(<var>x</var> + 5) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 8 or <var>x</var> = −5.
Divide both sides by 5: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 2<var>x</var> − 15 = 0, so (<var>x</var> − 5)(<var>x</var> + 3) = 0 and <var>x</var> = 5 or <var>x</var> = −3.

questions.t: Solve each equation by factorising. In part c, first divide both sides by the common factor.
p: 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 9<var>x</var> + 4 = 0
3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>x</var> + 6 = 0
20<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 70<var>x</var> + 60 = 0
ap: 2 × 4 = 8, and 8 + 1 = 9, so 2x2 + 8x + x + 4 = 2x(x + 4) + 1(x + 4) = (x + 4)(2x + 1) = 0. Hence x = −4 or x = −12.
3 × 6 = 18, and (−9) + (−2) = −11, so 3x2 − 9x − 2x + 6 = 3x(x − 3) − 2(x − 3) = (x − 3)(3x − 2) = 0. Hence x = 3 or x = 23.
Divide by 10: 2x2 − 7x + 6 = 0. Since 2 × 6 = 12 and (−3) + (−4) = −7, 2x2 − 3x − 4x + 6 = x(2x − 3) − 2(2x − 3) = (2x − 3)(x − 2) = 0. Hence x = 32 or x = 2.

questions.t: Complete the square for each expression.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> + 3
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 5<var>x</var> + 1
2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 12<var>x</var> − 5
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> + 3 = (<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> + 16) − 16 + 3 = (<var>x</var> + 4)<sup>2</sup> − 13.
x2 − 5x + 1 = (x2 − 5x + 254) − 254 + 1 = (x − 52)2 − 214.
2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 12<var>x</var> − 5 = 2(<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var>) − 5 = 2[(<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> − 9] − 5 = 2(<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> − 23.

questions.t: Solve each equation by completing the square. Give exact answers in surd form.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> − 4 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 5<var>x</var> + 2 = 0
2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> − 3 = 0
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> = 4, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> + 9 = 13 and (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> = 13. Hence <var>x</var> = −3 + √13 or <var>x</var> = −3 − √13.
x2 − 5x = −2, so x2 − 5x + 254 = −2 + 254 = 174 and (x − 52)2 = 174. Hence x = 5 + √172 or x = 5 − √172.
Divide by 2: x2 − 4x = 32, so x2 − 4x + 4 = 32 + 4 = 112 and (x − 2)2 = 112. Then x − 2 = ±√222, so x = 4 + √222 or x = 4 − √222.

questions.t: Use the quadratic formula to solve each equation. Give exact answers in simplest surd form.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>x</var> − 6 = 0
3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>x</var> − 4 = 0
2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 1 = 0
ap: a = 1, b = −4, c = −6, so Δ = 16 + 24 = 40. Then x = 4 ± √402 = 4 ± 2√102 = 2 + √10 or 2 − √10.
a = 3, b = 5, c = −4, so Δ = 25 + 48 = 73. Then x = −5 + √736 or x = −5 − √736.
a = 2, b = −6, c = 1, so Δ = 36 − 8 = 28. Then x = 6 ± 2√74 = 3 + √72 or 3 − √72.

questions.t: Solve each equation by first rearranging it into the form <var>ax</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>bx</var> + <var>c</var> = 0. Check that no solution you give makes a denominator zero.
p: x + 6x = 5
x + 23 = 8x
1x − 2 − 1x + 3 = 110
ap: Multiply by <var>x</var>: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6 = 5<var>x</var>, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 5<var>x</var> + 6 = 0 and (<var>x</var> − 2)(<var>x</var> − 3) = 0. Hence <var>x</var> = 2 or <var>x</var> = 3 (neither is 0).

Cross-multiply: <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 2) = 24, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var> − 24 = 0 and (<var>x</var> + 6)(<var>x</var> − 4) = 0. Hence <var>x</var> = −6 or <var>x</var> = 4 (neither is 0).

The left side is (x + 3) − (x − 2)(x − 2)(x + 3) = 5(x − 2)(x + 3), so (x − 2)(x + 3) = 50, giving x2 + x − 56 = 0 and (x + 8)(x − 7) = 0. Hence x = −8 or x = 7; neither is 2 or −3, so both are valid.

questions.t: For each equation, calculate the discriminant Δ = <var>b</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>ac</var>, then state how many solutions the equation has and, where solutions exist, whether they are rational or irrational. You do not need to solve the equations.
p: 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 7<var>x</var> + 3 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 4<var>x</var> + 9 = 0
9<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 30<var>x</var> + 25 = 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 2 = 0
ap: Δ = 49 − 24 = 25, which is positive and the square of a rational number, so there are two rational solutions.
Δ = 16 − 36 = −20 < 0, so there is no solution.
Δ = 900 − 900 = 0, so there is exactly one solution, and it is rational: x = −b2a = 3018 = 53.
Δ = 36 − 8 = 28, which is positive but not the square of a rational number, so there are two irrational solutions.

questions.t: The number of diagonals D of a polygon with n sides is given by D = n2(n − 3). How many sides does a polygon with 90 diagonals have?
questions.a: n2(n − 3) = 90, so n(n − 3) = 180 and n2 − 3n − 180 = 0. Factorising, (n − 15)(n + 12) = 0, so n = 15 or n = −12. A polygon cannot have −12 sides, so the polygon has 15 sides. Check: 152 × 12 = 90.

questions.t: A rectangular vegetable patch is 7 m longer than it is wide, and its area is 120 m<sup>2</sup>. Let the width be <var>x</var> m.
p: Write down an equation in <var>x</var> for the area of the patch.
Solve your equation, and hence state the width and the length of the patch.
ap: The length is (<var>x</var> + 7) m, so <var>x</var>(<var>x</var> + 7) = 120.

<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 7<var>x</var> − 120 = 0, so (<var>x</var> + 15)(<var>x</var> − 8) = 0 and <var>x</var> = −15 or <var>x</var> = 8. A width cannot be negative, so <var>x</var> = 8. The patch is 8 m wide and 15 m long. Check: 8 × 15 = 120.

questions.t: A cyclist rides 60 km at a constant speed. If she had ridden 5 km/h faster, the ride would have taken 1 hour less. Find her speed. (Introduce a pronumeral and say clearly what it stands for.)
questions.a: Let her speed be x km/h, so the ride takes 60x hours and the faster ride would take 60x + 5 hours. Then 60x − 60x + 5 = 1. Multiplying by x(x + 5): 60(x + 5) − 60x = x(x + 5), so 300 = x2 + 5x and x2 + 5x − 300 = 0. Factorising, (x + 20)(x − 15) = 0, so x = −20 or x = 15. A speed cannot be negative, so her speed is 15 km/h. Check: 60 ÷ 15 = 4 hours and 60 ÷ 20 = 3 hours, which is 1 hour less.

questions.t: Solve (<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>x</var>)<sup>2</sup> − 5(<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>x</var>) − 24 = 0 by first letting <var>u</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>x</var>. Give all four solutions exactly.
questions.a:
With u = x2 − 4x the equation becomes u2 − 5u − 24 = 0, so (u − 8)(u + 3) = 0 and u = 8 or u = −3.
If u = 8: x2 − 4x − 8 = 0, so (x − 2)2 = 12 and x = 2 + 2√3 or x = 2 − 2√3.
If u = −3: x2 − 4x + 3 = 0, so (x − 1)(x − 3) = 0 and x = 1 or x = 3.
The four solutions are x = 1, x = 3, x = 2 + 2√3 and x = 2 − 2√3. Check for x = 2 + 2√3: x2 − 4x = x(x − 4) = (2 + 2√3)(2√3 − 2) = 4(√3 + 1)(√3 − 1) = 4 × 2 = 8, and 82 − 5 × 8 − 24 = 0.

questions.t: This question is about the two numbers 4 − √7 and 4 + √7.
p: Find a monic quadratic equation with integer coefficients whose two solutions are 4 − √7 and 4 + √7.
Verify by substitution that <var>x</var> = 4 + √7 is a solution of your equation.
State the discriminant of your equation, and say what it tells you about the number and nature of the solutions.
ap: The required equation is (<var>x</var> − (4 − √7))(<var>x</var> − (4 + √7)) = 0, that is (<var>x</var> − 4)<sup>2</sup> − 7 = 0. Expanding: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> + 16 − 7 = 0, so <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> + 9 = 0. (Equivalently, the sum of the roots is 8 and the product is 16 − 7 = 9.)
Δ = (−8)<sup>2</sup> − 4 × 1 × 9 = 64 − 36 = 28. Since Δ > 0 there are two solutions, and since 28 is not the square of a rational number the two solutions are irrational.

questions.t: The number x satisfies x + 1x = 4.
p: Find the value of x2 + 1x2.
Hence find the value of x4 + 1x4.
Find the two exact values of <var>x</var>.
ap: Squaring both sides: (x + 1x)2 = x2 + 2 + 1x2 = 16, so x2 + 1x2 = 14.
Squaring again: (x2 + 1x2)2 = x4 + 2 + 1x4 = 142 = 196, so x4 + 1x4 = 194.
Multiplying x + 1x = 4 by x gives x2 + 1 = 4x, so x2 − 4x + 1 = 0 and (x − 2)2 = 3. Hence x = 2 + √3 or x = 2 − √3. Check: (2 + √3) + 12 + √3 = (2 + √3) + (2 − √3) = 4.

questions.t: Solve √(5x) − √(2x) = 3, giving the exact value of x. Your working will produce a second number that is not a solution: state which one it is and explain why it must be rejected.
questions.a:
Write √(5x) = 3 + √(2x) and square: 5x = 9 + 6√(2x) + 2x, so 3x − 9 = 6√(2x) and hence x − 3 = 2√(2x). Squaring again: x2 − 6x + 9 = 4 × 2x = 8x, so x2 − 14x + 9 = 0. Completing the square, (x − 7)2 = 49 − 9 = 40, so x = 7 + 2√10 or x = 7 − 2√10.
Because x − 3 = 2√(2x) ≥ 0, any solution must satisfy x ≥ 3. Now 7 − 2√10 ≈ 0.68 < 3, so 7 − 2√10 must be rejected — it was introduced by squaring. The only solution is x = 7 + 2√10. Check: x ≈ 13.325, so √(5x) ≈ √66.62 ≈ 8.162 and √(2x) ≈ √26.65 ≈ 5.162, and the difference is 3.

questions.t: Solve x − ax + a = x + a2x − a for x, where a is a positive constant. Give both solutions in terms of a, and check that neither makes a denominator zero.
questions.a: Cross-multiplying: (x − a)(2x − a) = (x + a)2, so 2x2 − 3ax + a2 = x2 + 2ax + a2. Hence x2 − 5ax = 0, so x(x − 5a) = 0 and x = 0 or x = 5a. Since a > 0, for x = 0 the denominators are a and −a, and for x = 5a they are 6a and 9a, so none is zero. Check x = 5a: LHS = 4a6a = 23 and RHS = 6a9a = 23. Check x = 0: LHS = −aa = −1 and RHS = a−a = −1.

questions.t: A rectangle is 1 unit wide and <var>x</var> units long, where 1 < <var>x</var> < 2. A square of side 1 unit is cut off one end, leaving a smaller rectangle whose sides are 1 unit and (<var>x</var> − 1) units. The smaller rectangle is similar to the original rectangle: the ratio of the longer side to the shorter side is the same for both.
p: Explain why the side of length 1 unit is the longer side of the smaller rectangle.
Show that <var>x</var> satisfies <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − <var>x</var> − 1 = 0.
Solve that equation, give the exact value of <var>x</var>, and check that it lies between 1 and 2.
ap: Since 1 < <var>x</var> < 2, subtracting 1 gives 0 < <var>x</var> − 1 < 1. So the side of length <var>x</var> − 1 is shorter than the side of length 1, which is therefore the longer side of the smaller rectangle.

For the original rectangle the longer side is x and the shorter side is 1, so the ratio is x1 = x. For the smaller rectangle the ratio is 1x − 1. The rectangles are similar, so x = 1x − 1. Multiplying both sides by x − 1 (which is not zero) gives x(x − 1) = 1, that is x2 − x = 1, so x2 − x − 1 = 0.

Completing the square: x2 − x + 14 = 1 + 14, so (x − 12)2 = 54 and x = 1 + √52 or x = 1 − √52. A length must be positive, so x = 1 + √52 ≈ 1 + 2.2362 ≈ 1.618, which does lie between 1 and 2. (This number is the golden ratio.)

questions.t: A closed rectangular box measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm.
p: Find its total surface area.
Find its volume.

questions.t: A cube has a total surface area of 294 cm<sup>2</sup>.
p: Find the length of one edge.
Find the volume of the cube.
ap: If the edge is <var>s</var> cm then 6<var>s</var><sup>2</sup> = 294, so <var>s</var><sup>2</sup> = 49 and <var>s</var> = 7 cm.
V = 7<sup>3</sup> = 343 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: A closed cylinder has base radius 4 cm and height 9 cm.
p: Find the area of its curved surface, in terms of π.
Find its total surface area, correct to two decimal places.
Find its volume, correct to two decimal places.
ap: Curved surface = 2π<var>rh</var> = 2π × 4 × 9 = 72π cm<sup>2</sup>.
The two circular ends add 2 × π × 4<sup>2</sup> = 32π cm<sup>2</sup>, so S = 72π + 32π = 104π ≈ 326.73 cm<sup>2</sup>.
V = π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup><var>h</var> = π × 16 × 9 = 144π ≈ 452.39 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: The cross-section of a right triangular prism is a right-angled triangle whose two shorter sides are 6 cm and 8 cm. The prism is 15 cm long.
p: Find the volume of the prism.
Find the total surface area of the prism.
questions.al: The hypotenuse of the triangle is √(6<sup>2</sup> + 8<sup>2</sup>) = √100 = 10 cm, and the area of the triangle is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm<sup>2</sup>.
ap: V = A<var>h</var> = 24 × 15 = 360 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: <var>VABCD</var> is a right square pyramid. The base <var>ABCD</var> is a square of side 10 cm, and the vertex <var>V</var> is 12 cm vertically above the centre <var>O</var> of the base.
p: Find the volume of the pyramid.
Let <var>M</var> be the midpoint of <var>BC</var>. Find the length <var>VM</var>, which is the height of the triangular face △<var>VBC</var>.
Find the total surface area of the pyramid.
ap: V = ⅓ × base area × height = ⅓ × 10<sup>2</sup> × 12 = 400 cm<sup>3</sup>.
<var>OM</var> = 5 cm (half the side of the square), and <var>VO</var> ⊥ <var>OM</var>, so <var>VM</var><sup>2</sup> = 12<sup>2</sup> + 5<sup>2</sup> = 144 + 25 = 169, giving <var>VM</var> = 13 cm.
Each of the four triangular faces has area ½ × 10 × 13 = 65 cm<sup>2</sup>, so S = 4 × 65 + 10<sup>2</sup> = 260 + 100 = 360 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A right cone has base radius 9 cm and height 12 cm.
p: Find the slant height of the cone.
Find the area of the curved surface, in terms of π.
Find the total surface area, including the base, correct to two decimal places.
Find the volume, correct to two decimal places.
ap: Slant height = √(9<sup>2</sup> + 12<sup>2</sup>) = √225 = 15 cm.
Curved surface = π × 9 × 15 = 135π cm<sup>2</sup>.
Base = π × 9<sup>2</sup> = 81π cm<sup>2</sup>, so S = 135π + 81π = 216π ≈ 678.58 cm<sup>2</sup>.
V = ⅓π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup><var>h</var> = ⅓ × π × 81 × 12 = 324π ≈ 1017.88 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: A sphere has radius 7 cm.
p: Find its surface area, in terms of π and then correct to two decimal places.
Find its volume, in terms of π and then correct to two decimal places.
ap: S = 4π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = 4π × 49 = 196π ≈ 615.75 cm<sup>2</sup>.
V = 43πr3 = 43π × 343 = 1372π3 ≈ 1436.76 cm3.

questions.t: A solid model has a total surface area of 50 cm<sup>2</sup> and a volume of 24 cm<sup>3</sup>. Every dimension of the model is then enlarged by a factor of 3.
p: Find the total surface area of the enlarged solid.
Find the volume of the enlarged solid.
ap: Surface area is multiplied by 3<sup>2</sup> = 9, so S = 9 × 50 = 450 cm<sup>2</sup>.
Volume is multiplied by 3<sup>3</sup> = 27, so V = 27 × 24 = 648 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: A closed cylindrical tin has base radius 5 cm and a volume of 750 cm<sup>3</sup>.
p: Find the height of the tin, correct to two decimal places.
Find the exact total surface area of the tin, then give it correct to two decimal places.
ap: π × 52 × h = 750, so h = 75025π = 30π ≈ 9.55 cm.
Curved surface = 2π × 5 × 30π = 300 cm2 exactly, and the two ends give 2π × 25 = 50π cm2. So S = (300 + 50π) cm2 ≈ 457.08 cm2.

questions.t: A model of a grain silo is built to a scale of 1 : 60, so that 1 cm on the model represents 60 cm on the real silo.
p: The outside of the model is covered with 250 cm<sup>2</sup> of foil. Find the area of steel sheet, in m<sup>2</sup>, needed to cover the outside of the real silo.
The real silo holds 108 m<sup>3</sup> of grain. Find the capacity of the model, in cm<sup>3</sup>.
ap: Areas are multiplied by 60<sup>2</sup> = 3600, so the real area = 250 × 3600 = 900 000 cm<sup>2</sup>. Since 1 m<sup>2</sup> = 10 000 cm<sup>2</sup>, this is 90 m<sup>2</sup>.
Volumes are multiplied by 60<sup>3</sup> = 216 000. Now 108 m<sup>3</sup> = 108 000 000 cm<sup>3</sup>, so the model's capacity = 108 000 000 ÷ 216 000 = 500 cm<sup>3</sup>.

questions.t: A right cone has base radius 6 cm and a total surface area, including its base, of 96π cm<sup>2</sup>.
p: Find the slant height of the cone.
Find the height of the cone.
Find the volume of the cone, in terms of π.
ap: π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + π<var>rl</var> = 96π gives 36π + 6π<var>l</var> = 96π, so 6<var>l</var> = 60 and the slant height is <var>l</var> = 10 cm.

questions.t: A solid is made of a cylinder of base radius 5 cm and height 12 cm, with a solid hemisphere of radius 5 cm sitting on top, so that the flat face of the hemisphere exactly covers the top circle of the cylinder.
p: Find the volume of the solid, in terms of π and then correct to two decimal places.
Find the total surface area of the solid, including the flat circular base, in terms of π and then correct to two decimal places.
ap: Cylinder: π × 52 × 12 = 300π cm3. Hemisphere: ½ × 43π × 53 = 250π3 cm3. Total V = 300π + 250π3 = 1150π3 ≈ 1204.28 cm3.

The surface consists of the flat base π × 5<sup>2</sup> = 25π, the curved cylinder 2π × 5 × 12 = 120π, and the curved hemisphere 2π × 5<sup>2</sup> = 50π. (The top circle of the cylinder is covered, so it is not counted.) S = 25π + 120π + 50π = 195π ≈ 612.61 cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A water trough is a prism 180 cm long, open at the top, lying so that its uniform cross-section is vertical. The cross-section is a trapezium whose two parallel sides are horizontal: the open top edge is 40 cm long, the bottom is 24 cm long, and the top and bottom are 30 cm apart vertically.
p: Find the capacity of the trough in litres, using 1000 cm<sup>3</sup> = 1 L.
The sheep on the farm drink 400 L of water each day. Find the smallest number of times the trough must be filled to the top each day.
ap: 400 ÷ 172.8 ≈ 2.31, so two fillings are not enough: the trough must be filled 3 times.

questions.t: A closed rectangular box has a square base. Its height is 4 times the side length of its base, and its volume is 500 cm<sup>3</sup>.
p: Find the side length of the base.
Find the total surface area of the box.
questions.al: Let the base have side <var>a</var> cm, so the height is 4<var>a</var> cm.
ap: V = <var>a</var><sup>2</sup> × 4<var>a</var> = 4<var>a</var><sup>3</sup> = 500, so <var>a</var><sup>3</sup> = 125 and <var>a</var> = 5. The base is 5 cm by 5 cm (and the height is 20 cm).

questions.t: A right cone has height <var>h</var> and base radius <var>r</var>.
p: Show that the total surface area of the cone, including its base, is π<var>r</var>(<var>r</var> + √(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>)).
Hence show that if the height of the cone is twice its radius, the total surface area is π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>(1 + √5).
ap: The height, the base radius and the slant height <var>l</var> form a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the centre of the base, so by Pythagoras' theorem <var>l</var><sup>2</sup> = <var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>, that is <var>l</var> = √(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>). The curved surface area is π<var>rl</var> and the base area is π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, so S = π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + π<var>r</var>√(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>) = π<var>r</var>(<var>r</var> + √(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>)).

If <var>h</var> = 2<var>r</var> then √(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>) = √(<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> + 4<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>) = √(5<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>) = <var>r</var>√5 (as <var>r</var> > 0). Hence S = π<var>r</var>(<var>r</var> + <var>r</var>√5) = π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>(1 + √5).

questions.t: A sphere of radius <var>r</var> fits exactly inside a closed cylinder, touching the top face, the bottom face and the curved surface of the cylinder.
p: Explain why the cylinder must have base radius <var>r</var> and height 2<var>r</var>.
Show that the volume of the sphere is exactly ⅔ of the volume of the cylinder.
Show that the surface area of the sphere is exactly ⅔ of the total surface area of the cylinder (curved surface plus the two circular ends).
ap: The horizontal cross-section of the sphere through its centre is a circle of radius <var>r</var>, and the sphere touches the curved surface all the way round, so that circle coincides with the cross-section of the cylinder: the base radius is <var>r</var>. The sphere also touches the top and bottom faces, so the distance between them equals the diameter of the sphere: the height is 2<var>r</var>.
Vcylinder = πr2 × 2r = 2πr3, and Vsphere = 43πr3. Then Vsphere ÷ Vcylinder = 43πr3 ÷ 2πr3 = ⅔, so Vsphere = ⅔ Vcylinder.

Curved surface of the cylinder = 2π<var>r</var> × 2<var>r</var> = 4π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, and the two ends give 2 × π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = 2π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, so the total is 6π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>. The sphere has surface area 4π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup>, and 4π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> ÷ 6π<var>r</var><sup>2</sup> = ⅔, as required.

questions.t: A right cone has base radius 12 cm and height 16 cm. A plane parallel to the base cuts the cone 8 cm above the base, and the small cone above the cut is removed, leaving a frustum.
p: Find the radius of the circular top of the frustum.
Find the exact volume of the frustum.
Find the exact area of the curved surface of the frustum.
Find the exact total surface area of the frustum, including both circular faces.
questions.al: The removed cone has height 16 − 8 = 8 cm, so it is an enlargement of the whole cone by a factor of 816 = ½.
ap: Radius of the top = ½ × 12 = 6 cm.
Whole cone: V = ⅓π × 12<sup>2</sup> × 16 = 768π cm<sup>3</sup>. Small cone: ⅓π × 6<sup>2</sup> × 8 = 96π cm<sup>3</sup>. Frustum = 768π − 96π = 672π cm<sup>3</sup>.

Slant height of the whole cone = √(12<sup>2</sup> + 16<sup>2</sup>) = √400 = 20 cm; of the small cone = √(6<sup>2</sup> + 8<sup>2</sup>) = 10 cm. Curved area = π × 12 × 20 − π × 6 × 10 = 240π − 60π = 180π cm<sup>2</sup>.
Add the two circles: 180π + π × 12<sup>2</sup> + π × 6<sup>2</sup> = 180π + 144π + 36π = 360π cm<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A right cone has vertex <var>V</var>, height <var>h</var> and base radius <var>R</var>, and its base has area <var>A</var>. A plane parallel to the base cuts the cone at a distance <var>x</var> from <var>V</var>, where 0 < <var>x</var> < <var>h</var>, giving a circular cross-section of radius <var>r</var> and area A<sub>x</sub>.
p: Use similar triangles to show that rR = xh.
Hence show that A<sub>x</sub> : <var>A</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> : <var>h</var><sup>2</sup>.
The cut is made at <var>x</var> = ½<var>h</var>. What fraction of the volume of the whole cone lies above the cut? Justify your answer.
Find, correct to three decimal places, the value of xh for which the cone above the cut has exactly half the volume of the whole cone.
ap: Let O be the centre of the base and P the centre of the cross-section, so V, P and O are collinear on the axis and VP = x, VO = h. Take a point Q on the cross-section circle and let B be the point where VQ produced meets the base circle. In △VPQ and △VOB: ∠PVQ = ∠OVB (same angle) and ∠VPQ = ∠VOB = 90° (the axis is perpendicular to both parallel circles), so the triangles are similar (AA). Hence PQOB = VPVO, that is rR = xh.
Ax : A = πr2 : πR2 = r2 : R2, and since rR = xh we get r2R2 = x2h2, so Ax : A = x2 : h2.

The cone above the cut is an enlargement of the whole cone by the factor xh = ½, so its volume is (½)3 = 18 of the whole. Checking directly: it has radius ½R and height ½h, so its volume is ⅓π(½R)2(½h) = 18 × ⅓πR2h. The fraction above the cut is 18.
The small cone is an enlargement by factor xh, so its volume is (xh)3 of the whole. We need (xh)3 = ½, so xh = 3√(½) = 13√2 ≈ 0.794 (0.7937 to four decimal places).

questions.t: For each parabola, state the axis of symmetry, the coordinates of the vertex, and the <var>y</var>-intercept.
p: <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> − 5)<sup>2</sup>
<var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> + 4)<sup>2</sup> + 2
<var>y</var> = −(<var>x</var> − 6)<sup>2</sup> + 3
ap: Axis <var>x</var> = 5, vertex (5, 0); when <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = (−5)<sup>2</sup> = 25, so the <var>y</var>-intercept is 25.
Axis <var>x</var> = −4, vertex (−4, 2); when <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = 4<sup>2</sup> + 2 = 18.
Axis <var>x</var> = 6, vertex (6, 3); when <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = −(−6)<sup>2</sup> + 3 = −36 + 3 = −33.

questions.t: Write down the equation of the parabola obtained when the basic parabola <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> is:
p: translated 6 units to the left
translated 2 units to the right and 5 units up
reflected in the <var>x</var>-axis and then translated 3 units to the right and 4 units down
ap: <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> + 6)<sup>2</sup>
<var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> − 2)<sup>2</sup> + 5
Reflection gives <var>y</var> = −<var>x</var><sup>2</sup>, then the translation gives <var>y</var> = −(<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> − 4.

questions.t: Complete the square, then state the axis of symmetry and the coordinates of the vertex.
p: <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> + 21
<var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 5<var>x</var> + 3
ap: <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> + 16) + 21 − 16 = (<var>x</var> + 4)<sup>2</sup> + 5. Axis <var>x</var> = −4, vertex (−4, 5).
y = (x2 − 5x + 254) + 3 − 254 = (x − 52)2 − 134. Axis x = 52, vertex (52, −134).

questions.t: Consider the parabola <var>y</var> = −<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 6<var>x</var> − 5.
p: Write down the <var>y</var>-intercept.
Complete the square and hence state the axis of symmetry and the vertex.
Find the <var>x</var>-intercepts.
State the maximum value of <var>y</var>.
ap: When <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = −5, so the <var>y</var>-intercept is −5.
<var>y</var> = −[<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 5] = −[(<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> − 9 + 5] = −(<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> + 4. Axis <var>x</var> = 3, vertex (3, 4).

0 = −(<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> + 4 gives (<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 4, so <var>x</var> − 3 = 2 or <var>x</var> − 3 = −2, giving <var>x</var> = 5 or <var>x</var> = 1. (Check: −1 + 6 − 5 = 0.)
The parabola is upside down, so the maximum value of <var>y</var> is 4, at <var>x</var> = 3.

questions.t: Find the exact values of the <var>x</var>-intercepts of each parabola.
p: <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> − 7
<var>y</var> = 2(<var>x</var> − 1)<sup>2</sup> − 10
<var>y</var> = 6 − 4(<var>x</var> − 1)<sup>2</sup>
ap: (<var>x</var> + 3)<sup>2</sup> = 7, so <var>x</var> = −3 + √7 or <var>x</var> = −3 − √7.
2(<var>x</var> − 1)<sup>2</sup> = 10, so (<var>x</var> − 1)<sup>2</sup> = 5 and <var>x</var> = 1 + √5 or <var>x</var> = 1 − √5.
4(x − 1)2 = 6, so (x − 1)2 = 32, giving x − 1 = ±√62. Hence x = 1 + √62 or x = 1 − √62.

questions.t: Factorise each quadratic and hence find the <var>x</var>-intercepts of its graph.
p: <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 2<var>x</var> − 24
<var>y</var> = 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 11<var>x</var> − 4
<var>y</var> = 25 − 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup>
ap: <var>y</var> = (<var>x</var> + 6)(<var>x</var> − 4), so the <var>x</var>-intercepts are −6 and 4.
y = (3x + 1)(x − 4) (since 3x2 − 12x + x − 4 = 3x2 − 11x − 4), so the x-intercepts are −13 and 4.
y = (5 − 2x)(5 + 2x), so the x-intercepts are 52 and −52.

questions.t: For each parabola, calculate the discriminant Δ = <var>b</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>ac</var> and hence state how many <var>x</var>-intercepts the graph has. When there are two, say whether they are rational or irrational.
p: <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 11
<var>y</var> = 4<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 12<var>x</var> + 9
<var>y</var> = 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 5<var>x</var> − 1
<var>y</var> = 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 7<var>x</var> + 2
ap: Δ = 36 − 44 = −8 < 0, so there are no <var>x</var>-intercepts.
Δ = 144 − 4 × 4 × 9 = 0, so there is exactly one x-intercept (at x = 32).
Δ = 25 + 8 = 33 > 0, and 33 is not a perfect square, so there are two irrational <var>x</var>-intercepts.
Δ = 49 − 24 = 25 > 0 and 25 is a perfect square, so there are two rational x-intercepts (3x2 − 7x + 2 = (3x − 1)(x − 2), giving x = 13 and x = 2).

questions.t: Consider the parabola <var>y</var> = 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 12<var>x</var> + 23.
p: Use the formula x = −b2a to find the axis of symmetry, and hence find the vertex.
Write the equation in the form <var>y</var> = <var>a</var>(<var>x</var> − <var>h</var>)<sup>2</sup> + <var>k</var>.
State the minimum value of <var>y</var>, and explain why the parabola has no <var>x</var>-intercepts.
ap: x = −−122 × 2 = 3. When x = 3, y = 18 − 36 + 23 = 5, so the vertex is (3, 5).
y = 2[x2 − 6x + 232] = 2[(x − 3)2 − 9 + 232] = 2[(x − 3)2 + 52] = 2(x − 3)2 + 5.

Since 2(<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> ≥ 0, we have <var>y</var> ≥ 5 for all <var>x</var>, so the minimum value is 5. As <var>y</var> is never 0 there are no <var>x</var>-intercepts. (Check: Δ = 144 − 4 × 2 × 23 = −40 < 0.)

questions.t: Find the equation of each parabola.
p: The parabola has vertex (−1, 4) and passes through the point (2, 22).
The parabola has <var>x</var>-intercepts −3 and 5, and <var>y</var>-intercept −30.
ap: The equation has the form <var>y</var> = <var>a</var>(<var>x</var> + 1)<sup>2</sup> + 4. Substituting (2, 22): 22 = 9<var>a</var> + 4, so 9<var>a</var> = 18 and <var>a</var> = 2. Hence <var>y</var> = 2(<var>x</var> + 1)<sup>2</sup> + 4 (that is, <var>y</var> = 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 4<var>x</var> + 6).

The equation has the form <var>y</var> = <var>a</var>(<var>x</var> + 3)(<var>x</var> − 5). When <var>x</var> = 0, <var>y</var> = <var>a</var> × 3 × (−5) = −15<var>a</var> = −30, so <var>a</var> = 2. Hence <var>y</var> = 2(<var>x</var> + 3)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>x</var> − 30.

questions.t: Solve each quadratic inequality.
p: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 3<var>x</var> − 28 > 0
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 7<var>x</var> + 10 ≤ 0
−<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> − 12 ≥ 0
ap: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 3<var>x</var> − 28 = (<var>x</var> − 7)(<var>x</var> + 4), and this upright parabola has <var>x</var>-intercepts −4 and 7, so it is above the <var>x</var>-axis when <var>x</var> < −4 or <var>x</var> > 7.
<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 7<var>x</var> + 10 = (<var>x</var> + 2)(<var>x</var> + 5); the graph is at or below the <var>x</var>-axis for −5 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ −2.
Multiplying by −1 reverses the inequality: <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 8<var>x</var> + 12 ≤ 0, that is (<var>x</var> − 2)(<var>x</var> − 6) ≤ 0, so 2 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 6.

questions.t: In a right-angled triangle, one of the two shorter sides is 7 cm longer than the other, and the hypotenuse is 13 cm. Find the three side lengths.
questions.a: Let the shorter of the two legs be <var>x</var> cm, so the other leg is (<var>x</var> + 7) cm. By Pythagoras' theorem, <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + (<var>x</var> + 7)<sup>2</sup> = 13<sup>2</sup>, so 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 14<var>x</var> + 49 = 169, giving 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 14<var>x</var> − 120 = 0 and <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 7<var>x</var> − 60 = 0. Then (<var>x</var> + 12)(<var>x</var> − 5) = 0, so <var>x</var> = 5 or <var>x</var> = −12. A length cannot be negative, so <var>x</var> = 5. The sides are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm (check: 25 + 144 = 169).

questions.t: A rectangular chicken run is to be built against a long straight shed wall, with the wall forming one entire side of the rectangle. There is 84 m of fencing available for the other three sides, and all of it is used. Let <var>x</var> m be the length of each of the two sides perpendicular to the wall.
p: Explain why the side parallel to the wall has length (84 − 2<var>x</var>) m, and show that the area <var>A</var> m<sup>2</sup> is <var>A</var> = 84<var>x</var> − 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup>.
Find the value of <var>x</var> that gives the largest possible area, and state the dimensions and the largest area.
ap: The fence covers two sides of length <var>x</var> m and the one side parallel to the wall, so that side is (84 − 2<var>x</var>) m. Hence <var>A</var> = <var>x</var>(84 − 2<var>x</var>) = 84<var>x</var> − 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup>.

<var>A</var> = 0 when <var>x</var> = 0 or 84 − 2<var>x</var> = 0, that is <var>x</var> = 42. The graph of <var>A</var> against <var>x</var> is an upside-down parabola, so its axis of symmetry is the average of the intercepts, <var>x</var> = 21. Then 84 − 2 × 21 = 42, so the run is 21 m by 42 m and the largest area is 21 × 42 = 882 m<sup>2</sup>.

questions.t: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from ground level. Its height <var>h</var> metres, <var>t</var> seconds after release, is given by <var>h</var> = 20<var>t</var> − 5<var>t</var><sup>2</sup>.
p: Find the maximum height reached, and the time at which it occurs.
Find the times between which the ball is at least 15 m above the ground, and hence how long it spends at or above 15 m.
ap: <var>h</var> = 5<var>t</var>(4 − <var>t</var>), so <var>h</var> = 0 at <var>t</var> = 0 and <var>t</var> = 4. The graph is an upside-down parabola, so the axis of symmetry is <var>t</var> = 2. Then <var>h</var> = 40 − 20 = 20, so the maximum height is 20 m, reached after 2 seconds.

Require 20<var>t</var> − 5<var>t</var><sup>2</sup> ≥ 15, that is 5<var>t</var><sup>2</sup> − 20<var>t</var> + 15 ≤ 0, so <var>t</var><sup>2</sup> − 4<var>t</var> + 3 ≤ 0 and (<var>t</var> − 1)(<var>t</var> − 3) ≤ 0. Hence 1 ≤ <var>t</var> ≤ 3: the ball is at or above 15 m from 1 second to 3 seconds after release, a total of 2 seconds.

questions.t: Consider the quadratic expression 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> − 4. (You should first find its vertex.)
p: Find the maximum value of 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> − 4 for −3 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 0.
Find the minimum value of 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> − 4 for −3 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 0.
Find the maximum value of 3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 8<var>x</var> − 4 for 0 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 2.
questions.al: The axis of symmetry is x = −86 = −43, and the value there is 3 × 169 − 323 − 4 = 163 − 323 − 4 = −163 − 4 = −283. The parabola is upright, so this is the overall minimum.
ap: On −3 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 0 the maximum is at an endpoint. At <var>x</var> = −3: 27 − 24 − 4 = −1. At <var>x</var> = 0: −4. So the maximum is −1 (at <var>x</var> = −3), since <var>x</var> = −3 is further from the axis than <var>x</var> = 0.
The vertex value x = −43 lies inside −3 ≤ x ≤ 0, so the minimum is −283 (= −913).
On 0 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 2 the whole interval is to the right of the axis, so the expression is increasing; the maximum is at <var>x</var> = 2: 12 + 16 − 4 = 24.

questions.t: Consider the quadratic inequality <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + <var>c</var> ≤ 0. For each of the following solution sets, find the value or values of <var>c</var> that make that set exactly the solution set of the inequality.
p: −1 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 7
<var>x</var> = 3 and no other value
no values of <var>x</var> at all
questions.al: The graph of <var>y</var> = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + <var>c</var> is an upright parabola with axis <var>x</var> = 3, and <var>y</var> ≤ 0 exactly between the <var>x</var>-intercepts.
ap: The solution set is −1 ≤ <var>x</var> ≤ 7, so the <var>x</var>-intercepts are −1 and 7. (These are symmetric about <var>x</var> = 3, as required.) Then <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + <var>c</var> = (<var>x</var> + 1)(<var>x</var> − 7) = <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> − 7, so <var>c</var> = −7.

Only one solution means the parabola touches the <var>x</var>-axis, so Δ = 36 − 4<var>c</var> = 0 and <var>c</var> = 9. Then <var>x</var><sup>2</sup> − 6<var>x</var> + 9 = (<var>x</var> − 3)<sup>2</sup> ≤ 0 only at <var>x</var> = 3.
No solutions means the parabola is entirely above the <var>x</var>-axis, so Δ = 36 − 4<var>c</var> < 0, that is <var>c</var> > 9.

questions.t: A batter's batting average is the total number of runs scored divided by the number of times she was out. In one season a batter scored 2100 runs. If she had been out on exactly one more occasion (with the same 2100 runs), her average would have been 5 runs less. Find how many times she was out, and her average.
questions.a: Let n be the number of times she was out, so her average is 2100n. The condition gives 2100n + 1 = 2100n − 5. Multiplying through by n(n + 1): 2100n = 2100(n + 1) − 5n(n + 1), so 0 = 2100 − 5n2 − 5n, giving n2 + n − 420 = 0. Then (n + 21)(n − 20) = 0, so n = 20 (rejecting n = −21, which is impossible). Her average is 210020 = 105. Check: 210021 = 100, which is 5 less than 105.

questions.t: A piece of wire 60 cm long is cut into two pieces, of lengths <var>x</var> cm and (60 − <var>x</var>) cm, where 0 < <var>x</var> < 60. The piece of length <var>x</var> cm is bent to form a circle, and the other piece is bent to form a square.
p: Show that the total area enclosed by the two shapes is A = x24π + (60 − x)216 cm2.
Show that A is least when x = 60π4 + π, and find that least total area exactly and then correct to one decimal place.
ap: The circle has circumference x, so its radius is r = x2π and its area is πr2 = π × x24π2 = x24π. The square has perimeter 60 − x, so its side is 60 − x4 and its area is (60 − x)216. Adding gives the result.

Expanding, A = x24π + 3600 − 120x + x216, so A is a quadratic in x with a = 14π + 116 = 4 + π16π (positive) and b = −12016 = −152. The minimum is at x = −b2a = 152 ÷ 4 + π8π = 152 × 8π4 + π = 60π4 + π, as required (and this is between 0 and 60). For that x, 60 − x = 60(4 + π) − 60π4 + π = 2404 + π, so A = 3600π24π(4 + π)2 + 5760016(4 + π)2 = 900π + 3600(4 + π)2 = 900(π + 4)(4 + π)2 = 9004 + π. Since 4 + π ≈ 7.1416, the least total area is 9004 + π ≈ 126.0 cm2 (occurring when x ≈ 26.4 cm).

questions.t: Here is another way to locate the vertex of the parabola <var>y</var> = <var>ax</var><sup>2</sup> + <var>bx</var> + <var>c</var>, where <var>a</var> ≠ 0 and <var>b</var> ≠ 0. Consider the horizontal line <var>y</var> = <var>c</var>.
p: Show that the line y = c meets the parabola at exactly the two points (0, c) and (−ba, c).
Hence explain carefully why the axis of symmetry of the parabola is x = −b2a.
Use this method to find the axis of symmetry and the vertex of <var>y</var> = 2<var>x</var><sup>2</sup> + 10<var>x</var> − 3, and check your vertex by completing the square.
ap: Points of intersection satisfy ax2 + bx + c = c, so ax2 + bx = 0, that is x(ax + b) = 0. Hence x = 0 or x = −ba, and these are different because b ≠ 0. Substituting back, the y-value at each is c, giving exactly the two points (0, c) and (−ba, c).

The two points have the same y-value, so reflecting the parabola in its axis of symmetry swaps them; therefore the axis passes through the midpoint of the segment joining them. Its x-coordinate is the average 12(0 + (−ba)) = −b2a, so the axis is x = −b2a.

Here a = 2, b = 10, c = −3. The line y = −3 meets the parabola at (0, −3) and (−102, −3) = (−5, −3), so the axis of symmetry is x = 0 + (−5)2 = −52. Then y = 2 × 254 − 25 − 3 = 252 − 28 = −312, so the vertex is (−52, −312). Check: y = 2[x2 + 5x] − 3 = 2[(x + 52)2 − 254] − 3 = 2(x + 52)2 − 252 − 3 = 2(x + 52)2 − 312, which confirms the vertex.

questions.t: Find each of the following angles, giving a reason for each answer.
p: In △<var>ABC</var>, ∠<var>BAC</var> = 47° and ∠<var>ABC</var> = 68°. Find ∠<var>BCA</var>.
In △<var>PQR</var>, ∠<var>PQR</var> = 35° and ∠<var>QPR</var> = 84°. The side <var>QR</var> is produced beyond <var>R</var> to the point <var>S</var>. Find ∠<var>PRS</var>.
In △<var>LMN</var>, <var>LM</var> = <var>LN</var> and ∠<var>MLN</var> = 46°. Find ∠<var>LMN</var>.
ap: ∠<var>BCA</var> = 180° − 47° − 68° = 65° (angle sum of a triangle)
∠<var>PRS</var> = 35° + 84° = 119° (an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles); check: ∠<var>PRQ</var> = 180° − 119° = 61° and 35° + 84° + 61° = 180°
<var>LM</var> = <var>LN</var>, so ∠<var>LMN</var> = ∠<var>LNM</var> = (180° − 46°) ÷ 2 = 67° (base angles of an isosceles triangle)

questions.t: Answer the following questions about polygons.
p: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. How many sides does the polygon have?
Find the sum of the interior angles of a convex polygon with 13 sides.
Four of the angles of a hexagon are each 132°, and the remaining two angles are equal to each other. Find the size of each of those two angles.
ap: The exterior angles of a convex polygon add to 360°, so the number of sides is 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

The angle sum of a hexagon is (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. The four given angles total 4 × 132° = 528°, leaving 720° − 528° = 192°, so each of the remaining two angles is 192° ÷ 2 = 96°. Check: 528 + 96 + 96 = 720.

questions.t: In each part, decide whether the two triangles are congruent. If they are, write a congruence statement with the vertices in matching order and name the congruence test used. If they are not, explain why not.
p: In △<var>ABC</var>, <var>AB</var> = 8 cm, <var>BC</var> = 5 cm and ∠<var>ABC</var> = 62°. In △<var>PQR</var>, <var>PQ</var> = 5 cm, <var>QR</var> = 8 cm and ∠<var>PQR</var> = 62°.
In △<var>DEF</var>, ∠<var>DEF</var> = 40°, ∠<var>EFD</var> = 75° and <var>EF</var> = 9 cm. In △<var>XYZ</var>, ∠<var>XYZ</var> = 40°, ∠<var>YZX</var> = 75° and <var>YZ</var> = 9 cm.

△<var>GHI</var> is right-angled at <var>H</var>, with hypotenuse <var>GI</var> = 13 cm and <var>GH</var> = 5 cm. △<var>JKL</var> is right-angled at <var>K</var>, with hypotenuse <var>JL</var> = 13 cm and <var>KL</var> = 5 cm.
In △<var>MNP</var>, <var>MN</var> = 6 cm, <var>NP</var> = 6 cm and <var>PM</var> = 9 cm. In △<var>RST</var>, <var>RS</var> = 6 cm, <var>ST</var> = 9 cm and <var>TR</var> = 9 cm.
ap: The 8 cm side of one triangle must match the 8 cm side of the other, and likewise the 5 cm sides, with the 62° angle included between them in each case: <var>AB</var> = <var>RQ</var> = 8 cm, <var>BC</var> = <var>QP</var> = 5 cm and ∠<var>ABC</var> = ∠<var>RQP</var> = 62°. So △<var>ABC</var> ≅ △<var>RQP</var> (SAS).

∠<var>DEF</var> = ∠<var>XYZ</var> = 40°, ∠<var>EFD</var> = ∠<var>YZX</var> = 75°, and the matching sides <var>EF</var> = <var>YZ</var> = 9 cm (each joins the 40° vertex to the 75° vertex). So △<var>DEF</var> ≅ △<var>XYZ</var> (AAS).

The right angles at <var>H</var> and <var>K</var> match, the hypotenuses <var>GI</var> = <var>JL</var> = 13 cm match, and the sides <var>GH</var> = <var>LK</var> = 5 cm match. So △<var>GHI</var> ≅ △<var>LKJ</var> (RHS). (The third sides are each √(13<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup>) = 12 cm.)

Not congruent. The three sides of △<var>MNP</var> are 6, 6 and 9 cm, while the three sides of △<var>RST</var> are 6, 9 and 9 cm. The two sets of side lengths are different, so no matching of vertices can make all three pairs of sides equal.

questions.t: △<var>ABC</var> is similar to △<var>PQR</var>, with the vertices written in matching order. <var>AB</var> = 6 cm, <var>BC</var> = 9 cm, <var>CA</var> = 12 cm and <var>PQ</var> = 8 cm.
p: Write down the similarity ratio <var>PQ</var> : <var>AB</var> in simplest form.
Find the lengths of <var>QR</var> and <var>RP</var>.
ap: <var>PQ</var> : <var>AB</var> = 8 : 6 = 4 : 3.
Every length in △PQR is 43 of the matching length in △ABC, so QR = 9 × 43 = 12 cm and RP = 12 × 43 = 16 cm. Check: 8 : 12 : 16 = 6 : 9 : 12 (each ratio equals 4 : 3).

questions.t: A vertical stick 45 cm tall casts a shadow 36 cm long on level ground. At the same time of day, a vertical flagpole standing on the same level ground casts a shadow 14 m long. Assuming the sun's rays are parallel, find the height of the flagpole.
questions.a: Each object and its shadow form a right-angled triangle, and the angles of elevation of the sun are equal because the rays are parallel, so the two triangles are similar (AAA). Matching lengths are therefore in the same ratio: heightshadow = 4536 = 1.25. Hence the height of the flagpole is 1.25 × 14 = 17.5 m. Check: 17.5 : 14 = 1.25 = 45 : 36.

questions.t: In △<var>ABC</var>, the point <var>D</var> lies on the side <var>AB</var> and the point <var>E</var> lies on the side <var>AC</var>, with <var>DE</var> ∥ <var>BC</var>. Also <var>AD</var> = 8 cm, <var>DB</var> = 6 cm, <var>AE</var> = 12 cm and <var>DE</var> = 10 cm.
p: Explain why △<var>ADE</var> is similar to △<var>ABC</var>.
Find the length of <var>EC</var>.
Find the length of <var>BC</var>.
ap: ∠<var>DAE</var> = ∠<var>BAC</var> (the same angle) and ∠<var>ADE</var> = ∠<var>ABC</var> (corresponding angles, <var>DE</var> ∥ <var>BC</var>), so △<var>ADE</var> is similar to △<var>ABC</var> (AAA).
AB = 8 + 6 = 14 cm, so the similarity ratio of △ABC to △ADE is 148 = 74. Hence AC = 12 × 74 = 21 cm and EC = 21 − 12 = 9 cm.
BC = 10 × 74 = 17.5 cm. Check: ADAB = 814 = 47, AEAC = 1221 = 47 and DEBC = 1017.5 = 47.

questions.t: The intervals <var>AE</var> and <var>BD</var> intersect at the point <var>P</var>, so that <var>P</var> lies between <var>A</var> and <var>E</var> and also between <var>B</var> and <var>D</var>. The intervals <var>AB</var> and <var>DE</var> are parallel. Also <var>AP</var> = 3 cm, <var>PB</var> = 5.4 cm, <var>PE</var> = 4 cm and <var>ED</var> = 5 cm.
p: Explain why △<var>PAB</var> is similar to △<var>PED</var>.
Find the length of <var>PD</var>.
Find the length of <var>AB</var>.
ap: ∠<var>APB</var> = ∠<var>EPD</var> (vertically opposite angles) and ∠<var>PAB</var> = ∠<var>PED</var> (alternate angles, <var>AB</var> ∥ <var>DE</var>), so △<var>PAB</var> is similar to △<var>PED</var> (AAA).
The similarity ratio is PAPE = 34, and PB matches PD, so PBPD = 34, giving PD = 5.4 × 43 = 7.2 cm.
AB matches ED, so AB = 5 × 34 = 3.75 cm. Check: 3 : 5.4 : 3.75 = 4 : 7.2 : 5 (each pair in the ratio 3 : 4).

questions.t: <var>PQRS</var> is a square, with its vertices labelled in order around the square. <var>M</var> is the midpoint of <var>PQ</var> and <var>N</var> is the midpoint of <var>QR</var>.
p: Prove that △<var>SPM</var> ≅ △<var>SRN</var>.
Hence explain why <var>SM</var> = <var>SN</var>.
The square has side length 12 cm. Find the exact length of <var>SM</var>.
ap: In △<var>SPM</var> and △<var>SRN</var>: <var>SP</var> = <var>SR</var> (sides of a square); ∠<var>SPM</var> = ∠<var>SRN</var> = 90° (<var>M</var> lies on <var>PQ</var> and <var>N</var> lies on <var>RQ</var>, so these are the angles of the square at <var>P</var> and <var>R</var>); <var>PM</var> = ½<var>PQ</var> = ½<var>QR</var> = <var>RN</var>. So △<var>SPM</var> ≅ △<var>SRN</var> (SAS).
<var>SM</var> and <var>SN</var> are matching sides of congruent triangles, so <var>SM</var> = <var>SN</var>.
△<var>SPM</var> is right-angled at <var>P</var> with <var>SP</var> = 12 cm and <var>PM</var> = 6 cm, so <var>SM</var> = √(144 + 36) = √180 = 6√5 cm (≈ 13.4 cm).

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a parallelogram, with its vertices labelled in order around the parallelogram, and its diagonals meet at <var>O</var>. The point <var>X</var> lies on the side <var>AB</var> and the point <var>Y</var> lies on the side <var>CD</var>, and <var>X</var>, <var>O</var> and <var>Y</var> are collinear. Prove that <var>OX</var> = <var>OY</var>.
questions.a: In △<var>AOX</var> and △<var>COY</var>: <var>AO</var> = <var>CO</var> (the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other); ∠<var>OAX</var> = ∠<var>OCY</var> (alternate angles, since <var>AB</var> ∥ <var>DC</var> and <var>AC</var> is a transversal, with <var>X</var> on <var>AB</var> and <var>Y</var> on <var>DC</var>); ∠<var>AOX</var> = ∠<var>COY</var> (vertically opposite angles, since <var>X</var>, <var>O</var>, <var>Y</var> are collinear and <var>A</var>, <var>O</var>, <var>C</var> are collinear). Hence △<var>AOX</var> ≅ △<var>COY</var> (AAS), and so <var>OX</var> = <var>OY</var> (matching sides of congruent triangles).

questions.t: In △<var>ABC</var>, ∠<var>ABC</var> = 90°, <var>AB</var> = 9 cm and <var>BC</var> = 12 cm. The point <var>D</var> lies on <var>AC</var>, and <var>BD</var> ⊥ <var>AC</var>.
p: Find the length of <var>AC</var>.
Prove that △<var>ABD</var> is similar to △<var>ACB</var>.
Find the lengths of <var>AD</var> and <var>BD</var>.
ap: In △<var>ABD</var> and △<var>ACB</var>: ∠<var>BAD</var> = ∠<var>CAB</var> (the same angle, since <var>D</var> lies on <var>AC</var>) and ∠<var>ADB</var> = ∠<var>ABC</var> = 90°. So △<var>ABD</var> is similar to △<var>ACB</var> (AAA).
Matching sides give ADAB = ABAC = BDCB. From AD9 = 915, AD = 8115 = 5.4 cm. From BD12 = 915, BD = 10815 = 7.2 cm. Check with areas: ½ × 9 × 12 = 54 and ½ × 15 × 7.2 = 54.

questions.t: In △<var>ABC</var>, <var>AB</var> = 6 cm, <var>BC</var> = 7 cm and <var>CA</var> = 9 cm. The side <var>AB</var> is produced beyond <var>B</var> to the point <var>D</var> so that <var>BD</var> = 21 cm, and the side <var>AC</var> is produced beyond <var>C</var> to the point <var>E</var> so that <var>CE</var> = 9 cm.
p: Prove that △<var>ADE</var> is similar to △<var>ACB</var>.
Find the length of <var>DE</var>.
ap: AD = 6 + 21 = 27 cm and AE = 9 + 9 = 18 cm. Then ADAC = 279 = 3 and AEAB = 186 = 3, and ∠DAE = ∠CAB (the same angle, since D is on ray AB and E is on ray AC). So △ADE is similar to △ACB (SAS), with similarity ratio 3.
<var>DE</var> matches <var>CB</var>, so <var>DE</var> = 3 × 7 = 21 cm.

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a trapezium, with its vertices labelled in order around the trapezium, in which <var>AB</var> ∥ <var>DC</var>, <var>AB</var> = 15 cm and <var>DC</var> = 9 cm. The diagonals <var>AC</var> and <var>BD</var> meet at <var>O</var>, and <var>AC</var> = 20 cm.
p: Prove that △<var>OAB</var> is similar to △<var>OCD</var>.
Find the length of <var>AO</var>.
Write down the ratio <var>BO</var> : <var>OD</var>.
ap: In △<var>OAB</var> and △<var>OCD</var>: ∠<var>OAB</var> = ∠<var>OCD</var> (alternate angles, <var>AB</var> ∥ <var>DC</var>, transversal <var>AC</var>) and ∠<var>OBA</var> = ∠<var>ODC</var> (alternate angles, <var>AB</var> ∥ <var>DC</var>, transversal <var>BD</var>). So △<var>OAB</var> is similar to △<var>OCD</var> (AAA).
The similarity ratio is AB : CD = 15 : 9 = 5 : 3, so AO : OC = 5 : 3. Since AO + OC = AC = 20 cm, AO = 58 × 20 = 12.5 cm (and OC = 7.5 cm).
<var>BO</var> : <var>OD</var> = 5 : 3.

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a rectangle, with its vertices labelled in order around the rectangle, and <var>AB</var> = 24 cm and <var>BC</var> = 7 cm. The perpendicular from <var>B</var> to the diagonal <var>AC</var> meets <var>AC</var> at <var>E</var>, and the perpendicular from <var>D</var> to the diagonal <var>AC</var> meets <var>AC</var> at <var>F</var>.
p: Find the length of <var>AC</var>.
Prove that △<var>AEB</var> is similar to △<var>ABC</var>.
Find the length of <var>AE</var>.
Find the length of <var>EF</var>.
ap: ∠<var>ABC</var> = 90°, so <var>AC</var> = √(24<sup>2</sup> + 7<sup>2</sup>) = √625 = 25 cm.
∠<var>EAB</var> = ∠<var>BAC</var> (the same angle, since <var>E</var> lies on <var>AC</var>) and ∠<var>AEB</var> = ∠<var>ABC</var> = 90°, so △<var>AEB</var> is similar to △<var>ABC</var> (AAA).
Matching sides give AEAB = ABAC, so AE = 24 × 2425 = 57625 = 23.04 cm.

In △ADC, ∠ADC = 90° and AD = BC = 7 cm, and the same argument gives △AFD similar to △ADC, so AF = AD2AC = 4925 = 1.96 cm. Since 1.96 < 23.04, F lies between A and E, so EF = AE − AF = 23.04 − 1.96 = 21.08 cm. Check: by symmetry CE = AF = 1.96 cm, and 1.96 + 21.08 + 1.96 = 25 = AC.

questions.t: The cross-section of a tent is the triangle <var>ABC</var>, where <var>AB</var> = <var>AC</var> = 5 m and <var>BC</var> = 6 m, and <var>BC</var> lies on horizontal ground. The point <var>X</var> is the midpoint of <var>BC</var>.
p: Explain why <var>AX</var> ⊥ <var>BC</var>, and find the length of <var>AX</var>.

A rectangle <var>PQRS</var> is drawn inside the triangle, with <var>P</var> and <var>S</var> on <var>BC</var>, <var>Q</var> on <var>AB</var> and <var>R</var> on <var>AC</var>, so that <var>QR</var> ∥ <var>BC</var> and the rectangle is symmetrical about <var>AX</var>. Given that <var>QR</var> = 3.6 m, find the height <var>PQ</var> of the rectangle.
A square is now drawn standing on <var>QR</var>, symmetrical about <var>AX</var>, with its two upper vertices lying on <var>AB</var> and <var>AC</var>. Find the side length of this square.
ap: △<var>ABX</var> ≅ △<var>ACX</var> (SSS: <var>AB</var> = <var>AC</var>, <var>BX</var> = <var>CX</var>, <var>AX</var> common), so ∠<var>AXB</var> = ∠<var>AXC</var>; as these add to 180° each is 90°. Then <var>AX</var> = √(5<sup>2</sup> − 3<sup>2</sup>) = √16 = 4 m.
Since QR ∥ BC, △AQR is similar to △ABC (AAA), with ratio QRBC = 3.66 = 0.6. The distance from A to QR is therefore 0.6 × 4 = 2.4 m, so PQ = 4 − 2.4 = 1.6 m.

Let the side of the square be s metres. The width of the triangle at a distance d from A, measured along AX, is 6 × d4 = 1.5d (similar triangles). The top of the square is at distance d = 4 − 1.6 − s = 2.4 − s from A, and its width is s, so s = 1.5(2.4 − s) = 3.6 − 1.5s. Then 2.5s = 3.6 and s = 1.44 m. Check: at d = 2.4 − 1.44 = 0.96 the width is 1.5 × 0.96 = 1.44, as required, and 1.44 < 3.6, so the square does fit on QR.

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a square, with its vertices labelled in order around the square, and its diagonals <var>AC</var> and <var>BD</var> meet at <var>O</var>. The bisector of ∠<var>BAC</var> meets <var>BO</var> at <var>X</var> and meets <var>BC</var> at <var>Y</var>. Prove that <var>CY</var> = 2 × <var>OX</var>.
questions.a: Let the square have side length a. Since the diagonals of a square are perpendicular, ∠AOX = 90° (X lies on OB), and ∠ABY = 90° (Y lies on BC). Also A, X and Y are collinear, since X and Y both lie on the bisector of ∠BAC, and O lies on AC, so ∠OAX = ∠BAY (each is half of ∠BAC). Hence △AOX is similar to △ABY (AAA), so OXBY = AOAB. Now AC = a√2 (Pythagoras) and AO = ½AC, so AOAB = 1√2, giving BY = √2 × OX. Next, let the perpendicular from Y to AC have foot P. In △ABY and △APY: ∠BAY = ∠PAY, ∠ABY = ∠APY = 90°, and AY is common, so △ABY ≅ △APY (AAS) and YP = YB. In △YPC, ∠YPC = 90° and ∠YCP = ∠BCA = 45° (the diagonal of a square bisects the right angle), so △YPC is right-angled and isosceles with PC = PY, giving YC = √2 × YP = √2 × YB. Therefore CY = √2 × (√2 × OX) = 2 × OX. (Numerical check with a = 1: BY = √2 − 1 ≈ 0.414, OX = 1 − 1√2 ≈ 0.293, CY = 2 − √2 ≈ 0.586 = 2 × 0.293.)

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a quadrilateral, with its vertices labelled in order around the quadrilateral. <var>P</var>, <var>Q</var>, <var>R</var> and <var>S</var> are the midpoints of <var>AB</var>, <var>BC</var>, <var>CD</var> and <var>DA</var> respectively. Prove that the intervals <var>PR</var> and <var>QS</var> bisect each other. (You may use the result that the interval joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length.)
questions.a: Join <var>AC</var>. In △<var>ABC</var>, <var>P</var> and <var>Q</var> are the midpoints of <var>AB</var> and <var>BC</var>, so <var>PQ</var> ∥ <var>AC</var> and <var>PQ</var> = ½<var>AC</var>. In △<var>ACD</var>, <var>S</var> and <var>R</var> are the midpoints of <var>AD</var> and <var>CD</var>, so <var>SR</var> ∥ <var>AC</var> and <var>SR</var> = ½<var>AC</var>. Hence <var>PQ</var> ∥ <var>SR</var> and <var>PQ</var> = <var>SR</var>. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram, so <var>PQRS</var> is a parallelogram. Its diagonals are <var>PR</var> and <var>QS</var>, and the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so <var>PR</var> and <var>QS</var> bisect each other.

questions.t: <var>ABCD</var> is a parallelogram, with its vertices labelled in order around the parallelogram. <var>M</var> is the midpoint of <var>AB</var> and <var>N</var> is the midpoint of <var>BC</var>. Prove that the area of △<var>MBN</var> is one eighth of the area of the parallelogram <var>ABCD</var>.
questions.a: Let h be the distance from C to the line AB, so that the area of the parallelogram is AB × h. Let G be the foot of the perpendicular from C to the line AB, and let H be the foot of the perpendicular from N to the line AB, so that CG = h. Now NH ∥ CG (both are perpendicular to AB), so in △BCG we have ∠BHN = ∠BGC = 90° and ∠NBH = ∠CBG (the same angle), giving △BNH similar to △BCG (AAA) with similarity ratio BNBC = ½. Hence NH = ½h. Taking MB as the base of △MBN, its height is NH, so its area is ½ × MB × NH = ½ × ½AB × ½h = 18 × AB × h, which is one eighth of the area of ABCD.

questions.t: In △<var>PQR</var>, the bisector of ∠<var>QPR</var> meets the side <var>QR</var> at <var>S</var>.
p: Prove that <var>QS</var> : <var>SR</var> = <var>PQ</var> : <var>PR</var>. (Hint: let the line through <var>R</var> parallel to <var>PS</var> meet <var>QP</var> produced beyond <var>P</var> at <var>T</var>, and show that <var>PT</var> = <var>PR</var>.)

In a triangle <var>PQR</var> with <var>PQ</var> = 10 cm, <var>PR</var> = 15 cm and <var>QR</var> = 8 cm, the bisector of ∠<var>QPR</var> meets <var>QR</var> at <var>S</var>. Find the length of <var>QS</var>.
ap: Let the line through R parallel to PS meet QP produced beyond P at T. In △QRT, the point S lies on QR and P lies on QT, with PS ∥ TR. Then ∠QSP = ∠QRT (corresponding angles) and ∠SQP = ∠RQT (the same angle), so △QSP is similar to △QRT (AAA) and QRQS = QTQP. Subtracting 1 from each side, QR − QSQS = QT − QPQP, that is SRQS = PTQP. Now ∠PTR = ∠QPS (corresponding angles, PS ∥ TR, transversal QT) and ∠PRT = ∠SPR (alternate angles, PS ∥ TR, transversal PR). Since PS bisects ∠QPR, ∠QPS = ∠SPR, so ∠PTR = ∠PRT and therefore △PTR is isosceles with PT = PR. Substituting, SRQS = PRPQ, that is QS : SR = PQ : PR.
QS : SR = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3, and QS + SR = 8 cm, so QS = 25 × 8 = 3.2 cm (and SR = 4.8 cm). Check: 3.2 : 4.8 = 2 : 3.

questions.t: Evaluate each of the following. Assume every pronumeral is non-zero.
p: 3<sup>4</sup>
2<sup>7</sup>
5<sup>−2</sup>
(43)−2
7 + <var>a</var><sup>0</sup>
(5<var>b</var>)<sup>0</sup>
ap: 5−2 = 152 = 125
(43)−2 = (34)2 = 916
<var>a</var><sup>0</sup> = 1, so 7 + <var>a</var><sup>0</sup> = 8
(5<var>b</var>)<sup>0</sup> = 1 (the whole product is raised to the power 0)

questions.t: Simplify each expression, writing every pronumeral in your answer with a positive index.
p: 3<var>a</var><sup>4</sup><var>b</var><sup>2</sup> × 5<var>a</var><sup>2</sup><var>b</var><sup>5</sup>
24x5y36x2y
(2<var>p</var><sup>3</sup><var>q</var><sup>2</sup>)<sup>4</sup>
(3<var>x</var><sup>2</sup><var>y</var>)<sup>−2</sup>
